question_en: Which woman, the daughter of his brother Germanicus, did Claudius take as his last wife?
derivation: Claudius married his niece Agrippina the Younger (daughter of his brother Germanicus, and Nero's mother), supported by 'inlecebris Agrippinae, Germanici fratris sui filiae ... cogendum se ad ducendum eam uxorem.' Entity-anchored, surfaces the brother-relation, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Liberos ex tribus uxoribus tulit: ex Vrgulanilla Drusum et Claudiam, ex Paetina Antoniam, ex Messalina Octaviam et quem primo Germanicum, mox Britannicum cognominavit.
question: Quos liberos Claudius ex uxore Messalina suscepit?
question_en: Which children did Claudius have by his wife Messalina?
derivation: Supported by 'ex Messalina Octaviam et quem primo Germanicum, mox Britannicum cognominavit.' Names both children; entity-anchored to Claudius and Messalina; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Antoniam Cn. Pompeio Magno, deinde Fausto Sullae, nobilissimis iuvenibus, Octaviam Neroni priuigno suo collocavit, Silano ante desponsam.
question: Cui Claudius filiam Octaviam in matrimonium collocavit?
question_en: To whom did Claudius give his daughter Octavia in marriage?
derivation: Supported by 'Octaviam Neroni priuigno suo collocavit.' Nero was his stepson, adopted son, and successor. Entity-anchored, single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: novas etiam commentus est litteras tres ac numero veterum quasi maxime necessarias addidit; de quarum ratione cum privatus adhuc volumen edidisset, mox princeps non difficulter optinuit ut in usu quoque promiscuo essent.
question: Quot novas litteras Claudius excogitavit et veterum numero addidit?
question_en: How many new letters did Claudius devise and add to the existing alphabet?
derivation: Claudius's three new letters added to the Latin alphabet, supported by 'novas etiam commentus est litteras tres ... addidit.' Number fact, entity-anchored, closed-book famous.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Historiam in adulescentia hortante T. Livio, Sulpicio vero Flauo etiam adiuuante, scribere adgressus est.
question: Quo auctore hortante Claudius adulescens historiam scribere adgressus est?
question_en: At whose urging did the young Claudius undertake to write history?
derivation: Supported by 'Historiam in adulescentia hortante T. Livio ... scribere adgressus est.' Entity-anchored to Claudius and Livy, single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Et veneno quidem occisum convenit; ubi autem et per quem dato, discrepat. Quidam tradunt epulanti in arce cum sacerdotibus per Halotum spadonem praegustatorem; alii domestico convivio per ipsam Agrippinam, quae boletum medicatum auidissimo ciborum talium optulerat.
question: Quo cibo medicato Claudius, ut plerique tradunt, veneno necatus est?
question_en: By which poisoned food, as most report, was Claudius killed?
derivation: The canonical account of Claudius's death by a poisoned mushroom offered by Agrippina, supported by 'veneno quidem occisum convenit ... per ipsam Agrippinam, quae boletum medicatum ... optulerat.' Entity-anchored, short answer, closed-book famous.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit III. Id. Octob. Asinio Marcello Acilio Auiola coss. sexagesimo quarto aetatis, imperii quarto decimo anno, funeratusque est sollemni principum pompa et in numerum deorum relatus; quem honorem a Nerone destitutum abolitumque recepit mox per Vespasianum.
question: Quoto aetatis anno Claudius decessit, ut Suetonius tradit?
question_en: In which year of his age did Claudius die, according to Suetonius?
derivation: Age-at-death fact, supported by 'sexagesimo quarto aetatis.' Ordinal answer, entity-anchored, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit III. Id. Octob. Asinio Marcello Acilio Auiola coss. sexagesimo quarto aetatis, imperii quarto decimo anno, funeratusque est sollemni principum pompa et in numerum deorum relatus; quem honorem a Nerone destitutum abolitumque recepit mox per Vespasianum.
question: Quoto imperii anno Claudius decessit, ut Suetonius tradit?
question_en: In which year of his reign did Claudius die, according to Suetonius?
derivation: Reign-length fact (AD 41-54), supported by 'imperii quarto decimo anno.' Ordinal answer, entity-anchored, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit III. Id. Octob. Asinio Marcello Acilio Auiola coss. sexagesimo quarto aetatis, imperii quarto decimo anno, funeratusque est sollemni principum pompa et in numerum deorum relatus; quem honorem a Nerone destitutum abolitumque recepit mox per Vespasianum.
question: Per quem principem Claudius honorem divinum a Nerone abolitum recepit?
question_en: Through which emperor did Claudius regain the divine honor that Nero had abolished?
derivation: Claudius was deified at death; Nero let the honor lapse and Vespasian restored it, supported by 'in numerum deorum relatus; quem honorem a Nerone destitutum abolitumque recepit mox per Vespasianum.' Entity-anchored (Claudius, Nero, Vespasian), single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Domitianus natus est VIIII. Kal. Novemb. patre consule designato inituroque mense insequenti honorem, regione urbis sexta ad Malum Punicum, domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.
question: Quo die natum esse Domitianum Suetonius tradit?
answer: Ante diem nonum Kalendas Novembres (VIIII Kal. Novemb.).
question_en: On what day does Suetonius say Domitian was born?
answer_en: On the ninth day before the Kalends of November (24 October).
derivation: Birth-date fact, anchored to Domitian. Supported verbatim by 'Domitianus natus est VIIII. Kal. Novemb.' Indirect statement (natum esse) under tradit. Closed-book: the birth-date (24 October AD 51) of a major emperor; short calendrical answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: regione urbis sexta ad Malum Punicum, domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.
question: In quod templum Domitianus domum, in qua natus erat, postea convertit?
question_en: Into what temple did Domitian later convert the house in which he had been born?
answer_en: Into the temple of the Flavian gens.
derivation: Building/family fact: Domitian's birth-house (in Rome's sixth region) was later turned into the Templum Gentis Flaviae, the dynastic shrine of the Flavians. Supported verbatim by 'domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; single named-monument answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: contrectatis multorum uxoribus, Domitiam Longinam Aelio Lamiae nuptam etiam in matrimonium abduxit, atque uno die super XX. officia urbana aut peregrina distribuit.
question: Quam feminam, Aelio Lamiae nuptam, Domitianus in matrimonium abduxit?
question_en: Which woman, married to Aelius Lamia, did Domitian carry off into marriage?
derivation: Family fact: Domitian's wife was Domitia Longina, whom he took from her husband Aelius Lamia. Supported verbatim by 'Domitiam Longinam Aelio Lamiae nuptam etiam in matrimonium abduxit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Aelius Lamia; single-name answer; closed-book (Domitia Longina, daughter of Corbulo, is the well-known empress).

author: Suetonius
source_text: habitabat cum patre una, sellamque eius ac fratris, quotiens prodirent, lectica sequebatur ac triumphum utriusque Iudaicum equo albo comitatus est.
question: Quo equo Domitianus triumphum Iudaicum patris fratrisque comitatus est?
question_en: On what horse did Domitian accompany the Jewish triumph of his father and brother?
derivation: Career detail: Domitian rode a white horse in the Jewish triumph of his father Vespasian and brother Titus (AD 71). Supported verbatim by 'triumphum utriusque Iudaicum equo albo comitatus est.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + the Jewish triumph; short, concrete answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: nec quicquam amplius quam muscas captare ac stilo praeacuto configere; ut cuidam interroganti, essetne quis intus cum Caesare, non absurde responsum sit a Vibio Crispo, ne muscam quidem.
question: Quid Vibius Crispus respondit interroganti num quis intus cum Domitiano esset?
question_en: What did Vibius Crispus reply to the man who asked whether anyone was inside with Domitian?
derivation: Famous joke: Domitian spent his hours stabbing flies, so when asked if anyone was with Caesar, Vibius Crispus quipped 'not even a fly.' Supported verbatim. Entity-anchored to Vibius Crispus + Domitian; the witticism survives translation; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Instituit et quinquennale certamen Capitolino Iovi triplex, musicum, equestre, gymnicum, et aliquanto plurium quam nunc est coronatorum.
question: In cuius dei honorem Domitianus quinquennale certamen triplex instituit?
question_en: In whose honor did Domitian establish a triple quinquennial contest?
derivation: Institutional fact: Domitian founded the quinquennial Capitoline Games (musical, equestrian, gymnastic) in honor of Capitoline Jupiter. Supported verbatim by 'quinquennale certamen Capitolino Iovi triplex.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Capitoline Jupiter; single-name answer; the Agon Capitolinus is a recognized institution.

author: Suetonius
source_text: De Chattis Dacisque post varia proelia duplicem triumphum egit.
question: De quibus gentibus Domitianus duplicem triumphum egit?
question_en: Over which peoples did Domitian celebrate a double triumph?
answer_en: Over the Chatti and the Dacians.
derivation: Military fact: a double triumph over the Chatti and the Dacians. Supported verbatim by 'De Chattis Dacisque ... duplicem triumphum egit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + named peoples; short list answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Bellum civile motum a L. Antonio, superioris Germaniae praeside, confecit absens felicitate mira.
question: Quis, superioris Germaniae praeses, bellum civile adversus Domitianum movit?
question_en: Who, as governor of Upper Germany, stirred up civil war against Domitian?
derivation: Historical fact: the revolt of L. Antonius Saturninus, governor of Upper Germany (AD 89), put down in Domitian's absence. Supported verbatim by 'Bellum civile motum a L. Antonio, superioris Germaniae praeside.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + the office; single-name answer (cognomen Saturninus supplied only in the gloss, not the text).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Iunium Rusticum, quod Paeti Thraseae et Helvidii Prisci laudes edidisset appellassetque eos sanctissimos viros; cuius criminis occasione philosophos omnis urbe Italiaque summovit.
question: Quos Domitianus, occasione damnati Iunii Rustici, urbe Italiaque summovit?
question_en: Whom did Domitian expel from Rome and Italy, on the occasion of the condemnation of Junius Rusticus?
derivation: Historical fact: Domitian's expulsion of philosophers from Rome and Italy, occasioned by the condemnation of Junius Rusticus (who had praised Thrasea Paetus and Helvidius Priscus). Supported verbatim by 'philosophos omnis urbe Italiaque summovit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Junius Rusticus; short answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Pari arrogantia, cum procuratorum suorum nomine formalem dictaret epistulam, sic coepit: "Dominus et deus noster hoc fieri iubet." Vnde institutum posthac, ut ne scripto quidem ac sermone cuiusquam appellaretur aliter.
question: Quibus verbis se appellari Domitianus voluit, cum epistulam procuratorum suorum nomine dictaret?
question_en: By what words did Domitian want himself to be addressed, when he dictated a letter in the name of his procurators?
derivation: Iconic fact: Domitian had himself styled 'dominus et deus,' beginning an official letter 'Our lord and god orders this,' and thereafter was addressed no otherwise. Supported verbatim. Entity-anchored to Domitian; the title survives translation; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Consulatus septemdecim cepit, quot ante eum nemo; ex quibus septem medios continuavit, omnes autem paene titulo tenus gessit.
question: Quot consulatus Domitianus cepit, quot ante eum nemo gesserat?
question_en: How many consulships did Domitian hold, more than anyone before him?
derivation: Number fact: Domitian held seventeen consulships, more than any predecessor. Supported verbatim by 'Consulatus septemdecim cepit, quot ante eum nemo.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; single-number answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Post autem duos triumphos Germanici cognomine assumpto Septembrem mensem et Octobrem ex appellationibus suis Germanico Domitianumque transnominavit, quod altero suscepisset imperium, altero natus esset.
question: In quae nomina Domitianus menses Septembrem et Octobrem transnominavit?
answer: Septembrem in Germanicum, Octobrem in Domitianum.
question_en: Into what names did Domitian rename the months of September and October?
derivation: Naming fact: Domitian renamed September 'Germanicus' (the month he had taken up the empire) and October 'Domitianus' (the month he was born). Supported verbatim by 'Septembrem mensem et Octobrem ... Germanico Domitianumque transnominavit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; short paired answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Per haec terribilis cunctis et invisus, tandem oppressus est amicorum libertorumque intimorum conspiratione, simul et uxoris.
question: Qua coniuratione Domitianus tandem oppressus est?
answer: Amicorum libertorumque intimorum, simul et uxoris.
question_en: By what conspiracy was Domitian at last overthrown?
answer_en: By a conspiracy of his intimate friends and freedmen, together with his wife.
derivation: Death fact: Domitian was killed by a palace conspiracy of his closest friends and freedmen, joined by his wife. Supported verbatim by 'oppressus est amicorum libertorumque intimorum conspiratione, simul et uxoris.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; short phrase answer; closed-book (the assassination of AD 96).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Stephanus, Domitillae procurator, et tunc interceptarum pecuniarum reus, consilium operamque optulit. Ac sinisteriore brachio, velut aegro, lanis fasciisque per aliquot dies ad avertendam suspicionem obvoluto, ad ipsam horam dolorem interiecit; professusque conspirationis indicium et ob hos admissus, legenti traditum a se libellum et attonito suffodit inguina.
question: Quis Domitiano, legenti libellum, primum vulnus intulit, inguina suffodiens?
question_en: Who struck the first blow at Domitian, stabbing him in the groin while he read a document?
derivation: Assassination fact: the steward Stephanus struck the first blow, stabbing Domitian in the groin as he read a handed-over document. Supported verbatim by 'Stephanus, Domitillae procurator ... legenti traditum a se libellum et attonito suffodit inguina.' Entity-anchored; single-name answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Occisus est XIIII. Kal. Octob. anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto, imperii quinto decimo.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Domitianus occisus est?
question_en: In which year of his age was Domitian killed?
derivation: Age-at-death fact. Supported verbatim by 'anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Domitian; closed-book (killed AD 96, aged 44/45). Source retains the Latin Library spelling 'quadragensimo' for 'quadragesimo.'

author: Suetonius
source_text: Occisus est XIIII. Kal. Octob. anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto, imperii quinto decimo.
question: Quoto imperii anno Domitianus occisus est?
question_en: In which year of his reign was Domitian killed?
derivation: Reign-length fact: Domitian was killed in the fifteenth year of his reign (AD 81-96). Supported verbatim by 'imperii quinto decimo.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Domitian; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Contra senatus adeo laetatus est, ut repleta certatim curia non temperaret, quin mortuum contumeliosissimo atque acerbissimo adclamationum genere laceraret, scalas etiam inferri clipeosque et imagines eius coram detrahi et ibidem solo affligi iuberet, novissime eradendos ubique titulos abolendamque omnes memoriam decerneret.
question: Quid senatus de Domitiano occiso decrevit, titulos eius ubique eradi iubens?
question_en: What did the senate decree about the slain Domitian, ordering his inscriptions to be erased everywhere?
answer_en: That all memory of him be abolished (the damnatio memoriae).
derivation: Historical fact: the senate rejoiced at Domitian's death and decreed his inscriptions erased and all memory of him abolished (damnatio memoriae). Supported verbatim by 'novissime eradendos ubique titulos abolendamque omnes memoriam decerneret.' Entity-anchored to the senate + Domitian; short noun-phrase answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Progenies Caesarum in Nerone defecit; quod futurum, compluribus quidem signis, sed vel evidentissimis duobus apparuit.
question: In quo principe progeniem Caesarum defecisse Suetonius initio Vitae Galbae tradit?
question_en: In which emperor does Suetonius, at the start of the Life of Galba, report that the line of the Caesars came to an end?
derivation: The famous opening sentence of the Life. Entity-anchored to the Caesars and Nero; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'Progenies Caesarum in Nerone defecit.' Indirect statement (progeniem ... defecisse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: the Julio-Claudian line ended with Nero (AD 68), one of the most-quoted lines of this Life.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Neroni Galba successit nullo gradu contingens Caesarum domum, sed haud dubie nobilissimus magnaque et vetere prosapia.
question: Quis Neroni in imperio successit, nullo gradu Caesarum domum contingens?
question_en: Who succeeded Nero in the empire, though connected by no degree of kinship to the house of the Caesars?
derivation: Succession fact. Entity-anchored to Nero; answer supported verbatim by 'Neroni Galba successit nullo gradu contingens Caesarum domum.' Succedo + dative (Neroni). Closed-book: Galba, unrelated to the Julio-Claudians, was the first of the four emperors of AD 68-69.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Familiam illustravit Seruius Galba consularis, temporum suorum et eloquentissimus, quem tradunt Hispaniam ex praetura optinentem, triginta Lusitanorum milibus perfidia trucidatis, Viriatini belli causam exstitisse.
question: Quot Lusitanorum milia Servius Galba consularis, orator ille, in Hispania perfidia trucidasse traditur, unde Viriatini belli causa exstitit?
question_en: How many thousands of Lusitanians is Servius Galba the consular, that famous orator, said to have treacherously massacred in Spain, whence arose the cause of the Viriathic War?
derivation: Ancestor fact: the orator Servius Sulpicius Galba (consularis, cos. 144 BC), great ancestor of the emperor and bearing the same name, governing Spain after his praetorship slaughtered 30,000 Lusitanians by treachery, provoking the Viriathic War. Number answer supported verbatim by 'triginta Lusitanorum milibus perfidia trucidatis.' Personal passive 'traditur ... trucidasse.' Disambiguated from the emperor by 'consularis, orator'; entity-anchored to Servius Galba + Lusitanians + the Viriathic War. Closed-book: the massacre (151 BC) that ignited the Lusitanian/Viriathic war.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Vxores habuit Mummiam Achaiam, neptem Catuli proneptemque L. Mummi, qui Corinthum excidit.
question: Quam urbem L. Mummius, Mummiae Achaicae proavus, excidisse traditur?
question_en: Which city is Lucius Mummius, the great-grandfather of Mummia Achaica, said to have destroyed?
derivation: Ancestor fact in Galba's genealogy: Mummia Achaica (Galba's mother) was great-granddaughter (proneptis) of L. Mummius, who sacked Corinth. Answer supported verbatim by 'proneptemque L. Mummi, qui Corinthum excidit.' Entity-anchored to L. Mummius + Corinth; personal passive 'traditur ... excidisse.' Closed-book: the sack of Corinth (146 BC) is among the most famous events of Rome's conquest of Greece.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ser. Galba imperator M. Valerio Messala Cn. Lentulo cons. natus est VIIII. Kal. Ian. in villa colli superposita prope Tarracinam.
question: Prope quod Latii oppidum Galba imperator natus esse traditur?
question_en: Near which town of Latium is the emperor Galba said to have been born?
derivation: Birthplace fact. Entity-anchored to Galba; place answer supported verbatim by 'in villa colli superposita prope Tarracinam.' Personal passive 'natus esse traditur.' Closed-book: Galba was born in a villa on a hill near Tarracina, on VIIII Kal. Ian. (24 December, 3 BC) in the consulship of M. Valerius Messala and Cn. Lentulus.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Honoribus ante legitimum tempus initis praetor commissione ludorum Floralium novum spectaculi genus elephantos funambulos edidit.
question: Quod novum spectaculi genus Galba praetor ludis Floralibus edidit?
question_en: What new kind of spectacle did Galba, as praetor, put on at the games of Flora?
derivation: Career fact: as praetor, at the Floralia, Galba staged a novel spectacle of tightrope-walking elephants. Answer supported verbatim by 'novum spectaculi genus elephantos funambulos edidit.' Entity-anchored to Galba + the Floralia; verifiable, translatable, fact-seeking; self-contained source. Closed-book: a noted anecdote of Galba's early career.

author: Suetonius
source_text: donec in oppido Fundis moranti Hispania Tarraconensis oblata est.
question: Quae provincia Galbae, Fundis moranti, oblata est, quam ante principatum administravit?
question_en: Which province was offered to Galba while he was staying at Fundi, which he governed before becoming emperor?
derivation: Governorship fact. Entity-anchored to Galba; province answer supported verbatim by 'Hispania Tarraconensis oblata est.' Closed-book and central to Galba's career: it was as governor of Hispania Tarraconensis that he was hailed emperor in AD 68.

author: Suetonius
source_text: consalutatusque imperator legatum se senatus ac populi R. professus est.
question: Quem se esse Galba, imperator consalutatus, professus est, priusquam Caesaris nomen sumeret?
question_en: What did Galba, when hailed emperor, declare himself to be, before he took the name of Caesar?
answer_en: The legate of the Senate and People of Rome.
derivation: Accession fact: saluted imperator in Spain, Galba professed himself merely 'legate of the senate and Roman people,' assuming the name Caesar only later, after Nero's death (ch. 11). Answer supported verbatim by 'legatum se senatus ac populi R. professus est.' Indirect statement (se esse) under professus est; entity-anchored to Galba; translatable. Closed-book: a famous detail of Galba's restrained accession.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Pisonem Frugi Licinianum, nobilem egregiumque iuvenem ac sibi olim probatissimum testamentoque semper in bona et nomen adscitum repente e media salutantium turba adprehendit filiumque appellans perduxit in castra ac pro contione adoptavit.
question: Quem Galba sibi successorem, filium appellans, in castris adoptavit?
question_en: Whom did Galba, calling him his son, adopt in the camp as his successor?
derivation: Succession fact: Galba adopted Piso Licinianus as his heir and successor before the troops. Answer supported verbatim by 'Pisonem Frugi Licinianum ... perduxit in castra ac pro contione adoptavit.' Entity-anchored to Galba + Piso; single-name answer. Closed-book: the adoption (10 January AD 69) that precipitated Otho's coup.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Quo faciliorem occasionem M. Salvio Othoni praebuit perficiendi conata intra sextum adoptionis diem.
question: Intra quotum a Pisonis adoptione diem M. Salvius Otho conata sua perfecit?
question_en: Within which day after the adoption of Piso did Marcus Salvius Otho accomplish his designs?
derivation: Timing fact: Otho carried out his plot within the sixth day of Galba's adoption of Piso. Number answer supported verbatim by 'perficiendi conata intra sextum adoptionis diem.' Entity-anchored to Otho + the adoption. Closed-book: Galba adopted Piso on 10 January and both were killed on 15 January AD 69.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Iugulatus est ad lacum Curti.
question: Quo loco fori Romani Galba imperator trucidatus est?
question_en: At what spot in the Roman Forum was the emperor Galba slaughtered?
derivation: Death-place fact: Galba was cut down at the Lacus Curtius in the Roman Forum. Answer supported verbatim by 'Iugulatus est ad lacum Curti' (and confirmed by ch. 23, 'in parte fori, qua trucidatus est'). Entity-anchored to Galba; place answer. Closed-book: Galba's murder in the Forum on 15 January AD 69 by soldiers acting for Otho. (source_text retains the Latin Library spelling 'lacum Curti' for 'lacum Curtii'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Periit tertio et septuagesimo aetatis anno, imperii mense septimo.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Galba imperator periit?
question_en: In which year of his age did the emperor Galba die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact. Ordinal/number answer supported verbatim by 'tertio et septuagesimo aetatis anno.' Entity-anchored to Galba. Closed-book: Galba died in his seventy-third year, the oldest of the emperors of AD 68-69.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Periit tertio et septuagesimo aetatis anno, imperii mense septimo.
question: Quoto imperii mense Galba periit?
question_en: In which month of his reign did Galba die?
derivation: Reign-length fact. Number answer supported verbatim by 'imperii mense septimo.' Entity-anchored to Galba. Closed-book: Galba's reign was very short, ending in its seventh month (he was killed 15 January AD 69).

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Q. HORATIUS FLACCUS, Venusinus, patre ut ipse tradit libertino et exactionum coactore
question: Unde oriundus erat Horatius poeta?
question_en: Where was the poet Horace from?
derivation: Origin fact, supported verbatim by the opening ethnic 'Venusinus' (= of Venusia). Anchored to Horace, single place answer; his birth at Venusia is a canonical, closed-book fact of Latin literary biography.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Q. HORATIUS FLACCUS, Venusinus, patre ut ipse tradit libertino et exactionum coactore
question: Cuius condicionis fuit pater Horati, ut ipse poeta tradit?
question_en: What was the status of Horace's father, as the poet himself reports?
answer_en: A freedman (and a collector of payments).
derivation: Father's status fact, supported verbatim ('patre ... libertino et exactionum coactore'). Anchored to Horace; the attribution 'ut ipse poeta tradit' mirrors the source's 'ut ipse tradit'. That Horace's father was a freedman is among the best-known facts about the poet, hence closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: bello Philippensi excitus a Marco Bruto imperatore, tribunus militum meruit; victisque partibus venia impetrata scriptum quaestorium comparavit.
question: Quo munere militari Horatius bello Philippensi sub Marco Bruto functus est?
question_en: What military office did Horace hold at the war of Philippi under Marcus Brutus?
derivation: Office fact, supported verbatim ('tribunus militum meruit'). Anchored to Horace, Philippi and Brutus; single office answer. Horace's tribunate at Philippi is a standard biographical fact, hence closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: bello Philippensi excitus a Marco Bruto imperatore, tribunus militum meruit; victisque partibus venia impetrata scriptum quaestorium comparavit.
question: Sub quo imperatore Horatius bello Philippensi tribunus militum meruit?
question_en: Under what commander did Horace serve as a military tribune in the war of Philippi?
derivation: Commander fact, supported verbatim ('excitus a Marco Bruto imperatore'). Anchored to Horace and Philippi; single-name answer. That Horace fought on the Republican side under Brutus at Philippi is a famous, closed-book fact.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Augustus epistolarum quoque ei officium optulit, ut hoc ad Maecenatem scripto significat:
question: Quod officium Augustus poetae Horatio obtulit?
question_en: What office did Augustus offer the poet Horace?
answer_en: The office of (his) secretary, in charge of his correspondence.
derivation: Office-offer fact, supported verbatim ('Augustus epistolarum quoque ei officium optulit'). Anchored to Augustus and Horace; the post of imperial secretary 'ab epistulis'. Horace declined it ('ne recusanti quidem aut suscensuit'), a well-known anecdote, hence closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Scripta quidem eius usque adeo probavit mansuraque perpetuo opinatus est, ut non modo Saeculare carmen componendum iniunxerit sed et Vindelicam victoriam Tiberii Drusique, privignorum suorum, eumque coegerit propter hoc tribus Carminum libris ex longo intervallo quartum addere;
question: Quod carmen Augustus Horatio componendum iniunxit?
question_en: What poem did Augustus charge Horace with composing?
derivation: Commission fact, supported verbatim ('Saeculare carmen componendum iniunxerit'); the subject of 'iniunxerit' is Augustus, established in the preceding context. Anchored to Augustus and Horace; that Augustus commissioned the Carmen Saeculare for the Secular Games is a canonical, closed-book fact.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Natus est VI Idus Decembris L. Cotta et L. Torquato consulibus, decessit V Kl. Decembris C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo consulibus post nonum et quinquagesimum diem quam Maecenas obierat, aetatis agens septimum et quinquagesimum annum, herede Augusto palam nuncupato, cum urgente vi valitudinis non sufficeret ad obsignandas testamenti tabulas.
question: Quibus consulibus Horatius poeta decessit?
answer: C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo.
question_en: In whose consulship did the poet Horace die?
answer_en: When Gaius Marcius Censorinus and Gaius Asinius Gallus were consuls.
derivation: Death-year fact (8 BC), supported verbatim ('decessit ... C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo consulibus'). Anchored to Horace, named consular pair; the consular dating frame parallels the reference Virgil file. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Natus est VI Idus Decembris L. Cotta et L. Torquato consulibus, decessit V Kl. Decembris C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo consulibus post nonum et quinquagesimum diem quam Maecenas obierat, aetatis agens septimum et quinquagesimum annum, herede Augusto palam nuncupato, cum urgente vi valitudinis non sufficeret ad obsignandas testamenti tabulas.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Horatius decessit?
question_en: In what year of his life did Horace die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact, supported verbatim ('aetatis agens septimum et quinquagesimum annum'). Anchored to Horace; single ordinal-number answer. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Natus est VI Idus Decembris L. Cotta et L. Torquato consulibus, decessit V Kl. Decembris C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo consulibus post nonum et quinquagesimum diem quam Maecenas obierat, aetatis agens septimum et quinquagesimum annum, herede Augusto palam nuncupato, cum urgente vi valitudinis non sufficeret ad obsignandas testamenti tabulas.
question: Post quotum diem ab obitu Maecenatis Horatius decessit?
question_en: How many days after the death of Maecenas did Horace die?
answer_en: On the fifty-ninth day after (59 days later).
derivation: Fact that Horace died shortly after Maecenas, supported verbatim ('post nonum et quinquagesimum diem quam Maecenas obierat'). Anchored to Horace and Maecenas; single number answer mirroring the source. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Natus est VI Idus Decembris L. Cotta et L. Torquato consulibus, decessit V Kl. Decembris C. Marcio Censorino et C. Asinio Gallo consulibus post nonum et quinquagesimum diem quam Maecenas obierat, aetatis agens septimum et quinquagesimum annum, herede Augusto palam nuncupato, cum urgente vi valitudinis non sufficeret ad obsignandas testamenti tabulas.
question: Quem Horatius heredem palam nuncupavit, cum testamenti tabulas obsignare non posset?
question_en: Whom did Horace name as heir by word of mouth, since he could not sign the tablets of his will?
derivation: Inheritance fact, supported verbatim ('herede Augusto palam nuncupato, cum ... non sufficeret ad obsignandas testamenti tabulas'). Anchored to Horace and Augustus; single-name answer; the oral nuncupation because too weak to sign is the precise detail Suetonius gives. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Horati)
source_text: Humatus et conditus est extremis Esquiliis iuxta Maecenatis tumulum.
question: Iuxta cuius tumulum Horatius in extremis Esquiliis humatus est?
question_en: Beside whose tomb was Horace buried at the far end of the Esquiline?
derivation: Burial fact, supported verbatim ('Humatus et conditus est extremis Esquiliis iuxta Maecenatis tumulum'). Anchored to Horace, Maecenas and the Esquiline; single-name answer. That Horace was buried next to Maecenas is a recognizable, closed-book fact.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Corneliam Cinnae quater consulis filiam duxit uxorem, ex qua illi mox Iulia nata est; neque ut repudiaret compelli a dictatore Sulla ullo modo potuit.
question: Cuius filiam Corneliam Caesar primam uxorem duxit?
question_en: Whose daughter Cornelia did Caesar take as his first wife?
derivation: First-wife fact: Cornelia, daughter of Cinna (consul four times); Caesar refused even Sulla's demand to divorce her. Anchored to Caesar + Cornelia + Cinna; single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: circa Pharmacussam insulam a praedonibus captus est mansitque apud eos non sine summa indignatione prope quadraginta dies cum uno medico et cubicularis duobus. nam comites seruosque ceteros initio statim ad expediendas pecunias, quibus redimeretur, dimiserat. numeratis deinde quinquaginta talentis expositus in litore non distulit quin e uestigio classe deducta persequeretur abeuntis ac redactos in potestatem supplicio, quod saepe illis minatus inter iocum fuerat, adficeret.
question: Quot talentis Caesar a praedonibus, qui eum circa Pharmacussam insulam ceperant, se redemit?
question_en: For how many talents did Caesar ransom himself from the pirates who had captured him near the island of Pharmacussa?
derivation: Ransom number, anchored to Caesar + pirates + Pharmacussa. Single verifiable number (quinquaginta talentis) in source; the famous pirate-capture episode. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: et in amitae quidem laudatione de eius ac patris sui utraque origine sic refert: 'Amitae meae Iuliae maternum genus ab regibus ortum, paternum cum diis inmortalibus coniunctum est. nam ab Anco Marcio sunt Marcii Reges, quo nomine fuit mater; a Venere Iulii, cuius gentis familia est nostra.'
question: A qua dea gentem Iuliam ortam esse Caesar in laudatione amitae suae Iuliae adfirmavit?
question_en: From which goddess did Caesar declare the gens Iulia descended, in the eulogy of his aunt Iulia?
derivation: From Caesar's funeral oration for his aunt Iulia (covers the aunt-Iulia ask). Indirect statement (gentem...ortam esse) under adfirmavit. Anchored to gens Iulia + Venus; single named answer, supported verbatim. Iconic (Venus Genetrix).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Deposita prouinciae spe pontificatum maximum petit non sine profusissima largitione; in qua reputans magnitudinem aeris alieni, cum mane ad comitia descenderet, praedixisse matri osculanti fertur domum se nisi pontificem non reuersurum. atque ita potentissimos duos competitores multumque et aetate et dignitate antecedentes superauit, ut plura ipse in eorum tribubus suffragia quam uterque in omnibus tulerit.
question: Quod sacerdotium amplissimum Caesar, duobus potentioribus competitoribus superatis, adeptus est?
question_en: Which supreme priesthood did Caesar obtain, defeating two more powerful competitors?
derivation: Office fact, anchored to Caesar; he won the pontificatus maximus over two older, more distinguished rivals. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Igitur cum Bibulo consul creatur.
question: Quo collega Caesar primum consulatum gessit?
question_en: With which colleague did Caesar hold his first consulship?
derivation: Colleague fact: Caesar's first consulship was shared with Bibulus (praenomen Marcus given earlier in the same chapter, 'Marcoque Bibulo'). Anchored to Caesar + consulship; iconic ('Iulius and Caesar' joke that follows). Single named answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sub idem tempus Calpurniam L. Pisonis filiam successuri sibi in consulatu duxit uxorem suamque, Iuliam, Gnaeo Pompeio conlocauit repudiato priore sponso Seruilio Caepione, cuius uel praecipua opera paulo ante Bibulum inpugnauerat.
question: Cuius filiam Calpurniam Caesar uxorem duxit?
question_en: Whose daughter Calpurnia did Caesar take as wife?
derivation: Marriage fact: Calpurnia, daughter of L. Piso (consul-designate to succeed Caesar). Anchored to Caesar + Calpurnia + Piso; single named answer supported verbatim.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sub idem tempus Calpurniam L. Pisonis filiam successuri sibi in consulatu duxit uxorem suamque, Iuliam, Gnaeo Pompeio conlocauit repudiato priore sponso Seruilio Caepione, cuius uel praecipua opera paulo ante Bibulum inpugnauerat.
question: Cui Caesar filiam suam Iuliam in matrimonium collocavit?
question_en: To whom did Caesar give his daughter Iulia in marriage?
derivation: Relation fact: Caesar married his daughter Iulia to Pompey (sealing the alliance). Anchored to Caesar + Iulia + Pompey; single named answer supported verbatim. Iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Germanos, qui trans Rhenum incolunt, primus Romanorum ponte fabricato adgressus maximis adfecit cladibus; adgressus est et Britannos ignotos antea superatisque pecunias et obsides imperauit.
question: Quis primus Romanorum, ut Suetonius tradit, Germanos trans Rhenum incolentes ponte fabricato adgressus est?
question_en: Who was the first Roman, according to Suetonius, to attack the Germans living across the Rhine by building a bridge?
derivation: 'primus Romanorum' fact, anchored to Germans + Rhine + bridge; the famous Rhine-bridge campaigns. Single answer (Caesar) decontextualized by the named entities. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: consecutusque cohortis ad Rubiconem flumen, qui prouinciae eius finis erat, paulum constitit, ac reputans quantum moliretur, conuersus ad proximos: 'etiam nunc,' inquit, 'regredi possumus; quod si ponticulum transierimus, omnia armis agenda erunt.'
question: Quod flumen prouinciae Caesaris finis erat, quo transito ille bellum ciuile incohavit?
question_en: Which river was the boundary of Caesar's province, by crossing which he began the civil war?
derivation: Geography/event fact: the Rubicon was the boundary of Caesar's province and the river of the civil war's start. Anchored to Caesar + province boundary; single named answer supported verbatim. Iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: tunc Caesar: 'eatur,' inquit, 'quo deorum ostenta et inimicorum iniquitas uocat. Iacta alea est,' inquit. atque ita traiecto exercitu, adhibitis tribunis plebis, qui pulsi superuenerant, pro contione fidem militum flens ac ueste a pectore discissa inuocauit.
question: Quod dictum Caesari tribuitur, cum exercitum trans Rubiconem traiceret?
question_en: What saying is attributed to Caesar as he led his army across the Rubicon?
derivation: Famous saying, anchored to Caesar + Rubicon crossing. Fact-seeking 'what did he say'; translatable ('the die is cast'); verbatim in source. Closed-book and iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Hinc urbe repetita in Macedoniam transgressus Pompeium, per quattuor paene menses maximis obsessum operibus, ad extremum Pharsalico proelio fudit et fugientem Alexandriam persecutus, ut occisum deprehendit.
question: Quo proelio Caesar Pompeium ad extremum fudit?
question_en: In which battle did Caesar finally rout Pompey?
derivation: Battle fact, anchored to Caesar + Pompey. Single named answer (Pharsalus) supported verbatim. Iconic, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Pontico triumpho inter pompae fercula trium uerborum praetulit titulum veni : vidi : vici non acta belli significantem sicut ceteris, sed celeriter confecti notam.
question: Quem titulum trium uerborum Caesar in triumpho Pontico inter pompae fercula praetulit?
question_en: What three-word placard did Caesar display among the floats at his Pontic triumph?
answer_en: 'I came, I saw, I conquered' (veni, vidi, vici).
derivation: The Pharnaces-victory dispatch, anchored to Caesar + Pontic triumph. Verbatim three-word answer; translatable; iconic. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Conuersus hinc ad ordinandum rei publicae statum fastos correxit iam pridem uitio pontificum per intercalandi licentiam adeo turbatos, ut neque messium feriae aestate neque uindemiarum autumno conpeterent; annumque ad cursum solis accommodauit, ut trecentorum sexaginta quinque dierum esset et intercalario mense sublato unus dies quarto quoque anno intercalaretur.
question: Quot dierum annum Caesar, fastos corrigens, ad cursum solis accommodavit?
question_en: To how many days did Caesar set the year when, reforming the calendar, he adjusted it to the course of the sun?
derivation: Calendar-reform fact (the Julian calendar), anchored to Caesar. Single number answer (365 days; intercalary day every fourth year) supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: non enim honores modo nimios recepit: continuum consulatum, perpetuam dictaturam praefecturamque morum, insuper praenomen Imperatoris, cognomen Patris patriae, statuam inter reges, suggestum in orchestra
question: Quod cognomen, ut Suetonius refert, inter nimios honores Caesari decretum est?
question_en: Which cognomen, according to Suetonius, was decreed to Caesar among his excessive honours?
derivation: Named-honour fact, anchored to Caesar; the same list also gives the perpetual dictatorship, continuous consulship, and praenomen Imperatoris. Single named answer (Pater patriae) supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: conspiratum est in eum a sexaginta amplius, Gaio Cassio Marcoque et Decimo Bruto principibus conspirationis.
question: Qui principes coniurationis in Caesarem fuerunt?
answer: Gaius Cassius et Marcus et Decimus Brutus.
question_en: Who were the leaders of the conspiracy against Caesar?
answer_en: Gaius Cassius, and Marcus and Decimus Brutus.
derivation: Assassination fact: 60+ conspirators, led by Cassius and the two Bruti. Anchored to Caesar + named ringleaders; verifiable named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: postquam senatus Idibus Martiis in Pompei curiam edictus est, facile tempus et locum praetulerunt.
question: In quam curiam senatus Idibus Martiis edictus est, ubi Caesar interfectus est?
question_en: Into which senate-house was the senate summoned on the Ides of March, where Caesar was killed?
answer_en: Into the Curia of Pompey (Pompey's senate-house).
derivation: Place-and-day fact: the senate met in Pompey's curia on the Ides of March, the murder scene. Anchored to Caesar + Ides of March; single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: atque ita tribus et uiginti plagis confossus est uno modo ad primum ictum gemitu sine uoce edito, etsi tradiderunt quidam Marco Bruto irruenti dixisse: kai su teknon
question: Quot plagis Caesar in curia confossus est?
question_en: With how many blows was Caesar stabbed in the senate-house?
derivation: Assassination number, anchored to Caesar. Single number answer (23 wounds) supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: atque ita tribus et uiginti plagis confossus est uno modo ad primum ictum gemitu sine uoce edito, etsi tradiderunt quidam Marco Bruto irruenti dixisse: kai su teknon
question: Quid Caesar Marco Bruto irruenti dixisse a quibusdam traditur?
question_en: What do some report Caesar said to Marcus Brutus as he rushed at him?
answer_en: 'Kai su, teknon' ('You too, child', in Greek).
derivation: Reported last words to Brutus, in Greek, attributed ('tradiderunt quidam'), anchored to Caesar + Marcus Brutus. Verbatim quote; fact-seeking 'what did he say'. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: sed nouissimo testamento tres instituit heredes sororum nepotes, Gaium Octauium ex dodrante, et Lucium Pinarium et Quintum Pedium ex quadrante reliquo; in ima cera Gaium Octauium etiam in familiam nomenque adoptauit
question: Quem Caesar novissimo testamento et in familiam nomenque adoptavit et ex dodrante heredem instituit?
question_en: Whom did Caesar in his last will both adopt into his family and name and make heir to three-quarters of his estate?
derivation: Succession fact: Caesar's will named Gaius Octavius principal heir (three-quarters) and adopted him. Anchored to Caesar + will + Octavius; single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Periit sexto et quinquagensimo aetatis anno atque in deorum numerum relatus est, non ore modo decernentium, sed et persuasione uolgi.
question: Quoto aetatis anno Caesar periit?
question_en: In which year of his age did Caesar die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact, anchored to Caesar. Single number answer (56th year) supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Annum agens sextum decimum patrem amisit; sequentibusque consulibus flamen Dialis destinatus dimissa Cossutia, quae familia equestri sed admodum diues praetextato desponsata fuerat, Corneliam Cinnae quater consulis filiam duxit uxorem.
question: Quoto aetatis anno Caesar patrem amisit?
question_en: In which year of his age did Caesar lose his father?
derivation: Biographical number fact, anchored to Caesar: he lost his father in his 16th year. Single number answer supported verbatim (annum agens sextum decimum). Closed-book, decontextualized.

author: Suetonius
source_text: sequentibusque consulibus flamen Dialis destinatus dimissa Cossutia, quae familia equestri sed admodum diues praetextato desponsata fuerat, Corneliam Cinnae quater consulis filiam duxit uxorem.
question: Quod sacerdotium adulescenti Caesari destinatum est?
question_en: To what priesthood was the young Caesar designated?
derivation: Office/priesthood fact, anchored to Caesar; he was designated flamen Dialis as a youth. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: flamen Dialis destinatus dimissa Cossutia, quae familia equestri sed admodum diues praetextato desponsata fuerat, Corneliam Cinnae quater consulis filiam duxit uxorem.
question: Cui Caesar praetextatus desponsatus fuerat, quam mox dimisit?
question_en: To whom had Caesar been betrothed as a boy, whom he then dismissed?
derivation: Betrothal fact: Caesar was betrothed as a boy to Cossutia (of an equestrian but wealthy family), then dismissed her to marry Cornelia. Anchored to Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim.

author: Suetonius
source_text: dum modo scirent eum, quem incolumem tanto opere cuperent, quandoque optimatium partibus, quas secum simul defendissent, exitio futurum; nam Caesari multos Marios inesse.
question: Quid Sulla, ut Suetonius tradit, de Caesare dixit, monens fore ut optimatibus quandoque exitio esset?
question_en: What did Sulla say about Caesar, according to Suetonius, warning that he would one day be the ruin of the optimates?
answer_en: That in Caesar there were many Mariuses.
derivation: Iconic saying attributed to Sulla when he spared Caesar. Anchored to Sulla + Caesar; verbatim quote (Caesari multos Marios inesse); fact-seeking 'what did he say', translatable. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Stipendia prima in Asia fecit Marci Thermi praetoris contubernio; a quo ad accersendam classem in Bithyniam missus desedit apud Nicomeden.
question: Sub quo praetore Caesar prima stipendia in Asia fecit?
question_en: Under which praetor did Caesar do his first military service, in Asia?
derivation: First-service fact, anchored to Caesar + Asia. Single named answer (Marcus Thermus) supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: reliqua militia secundiore fama fuit et a Thermo in expugnatione Mytilenarum corona ciuica donatus est.
question: Qua corona Caesar in expugnatione Mytilenarum donatus est?
question_en: With what crown was Caesar awarded at the storming of Mytilene?
derivation: Military-award fact, anchored to Caesar + Mytilene. Single named answer (corona civica) supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Meruit et sub Seruilio Isaurico in Cilicia, sed breui tempore.
question: Sub quo imperatore Caesar in Cilicia meruit?
question_en: Under which commander did Caesar serve in Cilicia?
derivation: Service fact, anchored to Caesar + Cilicia. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ceterum composita seditione ciuili Cornelium Dolabellam consularem et triumphalem repetundarum postulauit; absolutoque Rhodum secedere statuit.
question: Quem uirum consularem et triumphalem Caesar repetundarum postulauit?
question_en: Which ex-consul and triumphator did Caesar prosecute for extortion?
derivation: Prosecution fact, anchored to Caesar; his first great forensic case, against Dolabella for repetundae. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: absolutoque Rhodum secedere statuit, et ad declinandam inuidiam et ut per otium ac requiem Apollonio Moloni clarissimo tunc dicendi magistro operam daret.
question: Cuius rhetoris Rhodi Caesar operam dare statuit?
question_en: Under which rhetorician at Rhodes did Caesar decide to study?
derivation: Education fact, anchored to Caesar + Rhodes. Single named answer (Apollonius Molon) supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: huc dum hibernis iam mensibus traicit, circa Pharmacussam insulam a praedonibus captus est mansitque apud eos non sine summa indignatione prope quadraginta dies cum uno medico et cubicularis duobus.
question: Quot fere dies Caesar apud praedones, qui eum circa Pharmacussam ceperant, mansit?
question_en: About how many days did Caesar remain among the pirates who had captured him near Pharmacussa?
derivation: Number fact of the pirate-capture episode, anchored to Caesar + Pharmacussa. Single number (prope quadraginta dies) supported verbatim; distinct from the ransom fact. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sed et in ulciscendo natura lenissimus piratas, a quibus captus est, cum in dicionem redegisset, quoniam suffixurum se cruci ante iurauerat, iugulari prius iussit, deinde suffigi.
question: Quo supplicio Caesar piratas, a quibus captus erat, tandem adfecit?
question_en: With what punishment did Caesar finally punish the pirates who had captured him?
answer_en: Crucifixion (he had them strangled first, then crucified).
derivation: Punishment fact, anchored to Caesar + the pirates; he had sworn he would crucify them and did (strangled first for mercy). Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Tribunatu militum, qui primus Romam reuerso per suffragia populi honor optigit, actores restituendae tribuniciae potestatis, cuius uim Sulla deminuerat, enixissime iuuit.
question: Qui primus honor Caesari Romam reuerso per suffragia populi optigit?
question_en: What was the first office that came to Caesar by popular vote on his return to Rome?
derivation: Office fact, anchored to Caesar; the military tribunate was his first office won by popular vote. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: In Corneliae autem locum Pompeiam duxit Quinti Pompei filiam, L. Sullae neptem; cum qua deinde diuortium fecit adulteratam opinatus a Publio Clodio.
question: Quam Caesar in Corneliae locum uxorem duxit?
question_en: Whom did Caesar marry in Cornelia's place?
derivation: Marriage fact: after Cornelia's death Caesar married Pompeia (daughter of Q. Pompeius, granddaughter of Sulla). Anchored to Caesar + Pompeia; single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: cum qua deinde diuortium fecit adulteratam opinatus a Publio Clodio, quem inter publicas caerimonias penetrasse ad eam muliebri ueste tam constans fama erat, ut senatus quaestionem de pollutis sacris decreuerit.
question: Cuius adulterii suspicione Caesar Pompeiam uxorem repudiauit?
question_en: On suspicion of adultery with whom did Caesar divorce his wife Pompeia?
derivation: Divorce fact tied to the Bona Dea / Clodius scandal, anchored to Caesar + Pompeia + Clodius. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: interrogatusque, cur igitur repudiasset uxorem: 'quoniam,' inquit, 'meos tam suspicione quam crimine iudico carere oportere.'
question: Quid Caesar respondit, cum interrogaretur cur uxorem Pompeiam repudiasset?
answer: Meos tam suspicione quam crimine carere oportere.
question_en: What did Caesar answer when asked why he had divorced his wife Pompeia?
answer_en: That his household ought to be free from suspicion as much as from accusation.
derivation: The famous 'Caesar's wife must be above suspicion' saying, anchored to Caesar. Verbatim quote; fact-seeking 'what did he say', translatable. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: 'Amitae meae Iuliae maternum genus ab regibus ortum, paternum cum diis inmortalibus coniunctum est. nam ab Anco Marcio sunt Marcii Reges, quo nomine fuit mater; a Venere Iulii, cuius gentis familia est nostra.'
question: A quo rege Caesar maternum genus amitae suae Iuliae (Marcios Reges) ortum esse dixit?
question_en: From which king did Caesar say the maternal line of his aunt Julia (the Marcii Reges) descended?
derivation: From Caesar's funeral oration for his aunt Julia; the maternal (Marcii Reges) line traced to king Ancus Marcius. Anchored to Caesar + Marcii Reges; single named answer supported verbatim. Distinct from the Venus (paternal) fact. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Quaestori ulterior Hispania obuenit; ubi cum mandatu praetoris iure dicundo conuentus circumiret Gadisque uenisset, animaduersa apud Herculis templum Magni Alexandri imagine ingemuit.
question: Quae prouincia Caesari quaestori obuenit?
question_en: Which province fell to Caesar as quaestor?
derivation: Office/province fact, anchored to Caesar; as quaestor he was allotted Further Spain. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Gadisque uenisset, animaduersa apud Herculis templum Magni Alexandri imagine ingemuit et quasi pertaesus ignauiam suam, quod nihil dum a se memorabile actum esset in aetate, qua iam Alexander orbem terrarum subegisset.
question: Cuius imagine apud Herculis templum Gadibus conspecta Caesar ingemuit?
question_en: At whose statue, seen in the temple of Hercules at Gades, did Caesar sigh?
derivation: Iconic episode, anchored to Caesar + Gades + temple of Hercules; he sighed before Alexander's statue. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Aedilis praeter comitium ac forum basilicasque etiam Capitolium ornauit porticibus ad tempus extructis. uenationes autem ludosque et cum collega et separatim edidit. adiecit insuper Caesar etiam gladiatorium munus.
question: Quem magistratum gerens Caesar uenationes, ludos gladiatoriumque munus edidit et Capitolium ornauit?
question_en: Holding which magistracy did Caesar give wild-beast hunts, games, and a gladiatorial show, and adorn the Capitol?
derivation: Office fact, anchored to Caesar; as curule aedile he gave venationes, games, a gladiatorial show, and adorned the Capitol. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: quo factum est, ut communium quoque inpensarum solus gratiam caperet nec dissimularet collega eius Marcus Bibulus, euenisse sibi quod Polluci.
question: Quis Caesari collega in aedilitate fuit?
question_en: Who was Caesar's colleague in the aedileship?
derivation: Colleague fact: Bibulus was Caesar's colleague in the aedileship (as later in the consulship). Anchored to Caesar + aedileship; single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: quorum auctoritatem ut quibus posset modis in uicem deminueret, tropaea Gai Mari de Iugurtha deque Cimbris atque Teutonis olim a Sulla disiecta restituit.
question: Cuius imperatoris tropaea de Iugurtha et de Cimbris Teutonisque Caesar restituit?
question_en: Whose trophies over Jugurtha and over the Cimbri and Teutones did Caesar restore?
derivation: Political-gesture fact, anchored to Caesar; he restored the trophies of Marius (his relative) over Jugurtha, the Cimbri, and Teutones. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: cum mane ad comitia descenderet, praedixisse matri osculanti fertur domum se nisi pontificem non reuersurum.
question: Quid Caesar matri osculanti die comitiorum pontificatus dixisse fertur?
answer: Domum se nisi pontificem non reuersurum.
question_en: What is Caesar said to have told his mother, who kissed him, on the day of the pontifical election?
answer_en: That he would not return home except as pontifex.
derivation: Reported saying, anchored to Caesar + the pontifex maximus election. Acc.+inf. under 'fertur'; verbatim substance; translatable. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Praetor creatus, detecta coniuratione Catilinae senatuque uniuerso in socios facinoris ultimam statuente poenam, solus municipatim diuidendos custodiendosque publicatis bonis censuit.
question: Quem magistratum Caesar gerebat, cum coniuratio Catilinae detecta est?
question_en: Which magistracy was Caesar holding when Catiline's conspiracy was uncovered?
derivation: Office fact, anchored to Caesar + the Catilinarian conspiracy. Single named answer supported verbatim (Praetor creatus). Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: senatuque uniuerso in socios facinoris ultimam statuente poenam, solus municipatim diuidendos custodiendosque publicatis bonis censuit.
question: Quid Caesar unus de sociis coniurationis Catilinae censuit, cum senatus ultimam poenam decerneret?
answer: Eos municipatim distribuendos et custodiendos esse.
question_en: What did Caesar alone propose for the accomplices of Catiline's conspiracy, when the senate was decreeing the extreme penalty?
answer_en: That they be distributed among the towns and kept under guard (not executed).
derivation: Caesar's proposal in the famous Catilinarian debate (imprisonment vs. death), anchored to Caesar + the conspirators. Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: sed cum edictis iam comitis ratio eius haberi non posset nisi priuatus introisset urbem, et ambienti ut legibus solueretur multi contra dicerent, coactus est triumphum, ne consulatu excluderetur, dimittere.
question: Quid Caesar dimittere coactus est, ne consulatu excluderetur?
question_en: What was Caesar forced to give up so as not to be barred from the consulship?
derivation: Dilemma fact after his Spanish propraetorship: he had to forgo his triumph to stand for the consulship. Anchored to Caesar; single answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Pompeioque Marcum Crassum reconciliauit ueterem inimicum ex consulatu, quem summa discordia simul gesserant; ac societatem cum utroque iniit, ne quid ageretur in re publica, quod displicuisset ulli e tribus.
question: Cum quibus duobus uiris Caesar societatem iniit, ne quid in re publica ageretur ulli e tribus displicens?
question_en: With which two men did Caesar form an alliance, so that nothing should be done in the state displeasing to any of the three?
derivation: The First Triumvirate, anchored to Caesar; he reconciled Pompey and Crassus and joined both in a pact. Named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Inito honore primus omnium instituit, ut tam senatus quam populi diurna acta confierent et publicarentur.
question: Quid Caesar consul primus omnium instituit de senatus populique rebus cotidianis?
answer: Vt acta diurna confierent et publicarentur.
question_en: What did Caesar as consul first of all institute concerning the daily proceedings of the senate and people?
answer_en: That daily records (acta diurna) be compiled and published.
derivation: 'primus omnium' institution fact, anchored to Caesar's first consulship; he first had the acta diurna of senate and people published. Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: et initio quidem Galliam Cisalpinam Illyrico adiecto lege Vatinia accepit; mox per senatum Comatam quoque, ueritis patribus ne, si ipsi negassent, populus et hanc daret.
question: Qua lege Caesar Galliam Cisalpinam cum Illyrico accepit?
question_en: By which law did Caesar receive Cisalpine Gaul with Illyricum?
derivation: Law/province fact, anchored to Caesar; the lex Vatinia gave him Cisalpine Gaul with Illyricum. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Crassum Pompeiumque in urbem prouinciae suae Lucam extractos conpulit, ut detrudendi Domitii causa consulatum alterum peterent, perfecitque per utrumque, ut in quinquennium sibi imperium prorogaretur.
question: In quam urbem prouinciae suae Caesar Crassum et Pompeium extraxit, ut sibi imperium prorogaretur?
question_en: To which town of his province did Caesar draw Crassus and Pompey to have his command extended?
derivation: The conference of Luca, anchored to Caesar + Crassus + Pompey. Single named place answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: perfecitque per utrumque, ut in quinquennium sibi imperium prorogaretur.
question: In quot annos Caesari imperium, per Crassum et Pompeium, prorogatum est?
question_en: For how many years was Caesar's command extended, through Crassus and Pompey?
derivation: Number fact, anchored to Caesar; his Gallic command was extended for five years (in quinquennium). Single number answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: unam etiam ex Transalpinis conscriptam, uocabulo quoque Gallico Alauda enim appellabatur, quam disciplina cultuque Romano institutam et ornatam postea uniuersam ciuitate donauit.
question: Quo uocabulo Gallico appellabatur legio quam Caesar ex Transalpinis conscripsit?
question_en: By what Gallic name was the legion Caesar raised from Transalpine Gaul called?
derivation: Name fact, anchored to Caesar; the legion levied in Transalpine Gaul bore the Gallic name Alauda. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: adgressus est et Britannos ignotos antea superatisque pecunias et obsides imperauit.
question: Quos insulanos antea ignotos Caesar adgressus est, pecunias et obsides imperans?
question_en: Which previously unknown islanders did Caesar attack, exacting money and hostages?
derivation: Campaign fact, anchored to Caesar; he attacked the previously unknown Britons, imposing money and hostages. Single named answer supported verbatim; distinct from the Rhine-bridge (Germans) fact. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: per tot successus ter nec amplius aduersum casum expertus: in Britannia classe ui tempestatis prope absumpta et in Gallia ad Gergouiam legione fusa et in Germanorum finibus Titurio et Aurunculeio legatis per insidias caesis.
question: Ad quod oppidum Galliae una Caesaris legio fusa est?
question_en: At which town of Gaul was one of Caesar's legions routed?
derivation: Setback fact, anchored to Caesar; one of his three Gallic reverses was a legion routed at Gergovia. Single named place answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: et in Germanorum finibus Titurio et Aurunculeio legatis per insidias caesis.
question: Qui duo legati Caesaris in Germanorum finibus per insidias caesi sunt?
question_en: Which two of Caesar's legates were killed by treachery in the territory of the Germans?
derivation: Setback fact, anchored to Caesar; the legates Titurius and Aurunculeius (Sabinus and Cotta) were killed by treachery. Verifiable named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: munus populo epulumque pronuntiauit in filiae memoriam, quod ante eum nemo.
question: In cuius memoriam Caesar munus epulumque populo, quod ante eum nemo fecerat, edidit?
question_en: In whose memory did Caesar give the people a gladiatorial show and feast, something no one before him had done?
derivation: Novelty fact, anchored to Caesar; he gave a show and feast in memory of his daughter, first ever for a woman. Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: legionibus stipendium in perpetuum duplicauit.
question: Quid Caesar de stipendio legionum in perpetuum statuit?
question_en: What did Caesar permanently decide about the legions' pay?
derivation: Military-pay fact, anchored to Caesar; he permanently doubled the legions' pay. Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: regnum Aegypti uictor Cleopatrae fratrique eius minori permisit, ueritus prouinciam facere.
question: Cui Caesar uictor regnum Aegypti permisit?
question_en: To whom did Caesar as victor grant the kingdom of Egypt?
answer_en: To Cleopatra and her younger brother.
derivation: Settlement fact, anchored to Caesar + Egypt; after the Alexandrian war he gave the kingdom to Cleopatra and her younger brother. Named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: urgentibus de Pharnace nuntiis, quem Mithridatis Magni filium ac tunc occasione temporum bellantem iamque multiplici successu praeferocem, intra quintum quam adfuerat diem, quattuor quibus in conspectum uenit horis, una profligauit acie.
question: Quem Mithridatis Magni filium Caesar apud Pontum una acie profligauit?
question_en: Which son of Mithridates the Great did Caesar rout in a single battle in Pontus?
derivation: Victory fact, anchored to Caesar + Pontus; he crushed Pharnaces, son of Mithridates the Great, in one battle (the 'veni vidi vici' campaign). Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: dehinc Scipionem ac Iubam reliquias partium in Africa refouentis deuicit, Pompei liberos in Hispania.
question: Quos duces Caesar in Africa, reliquias partium refouentes, deuicit?
question_en: Which leaders, reviving the remnants of the party in Africa, did Caesar defeat?
derivation: Victory fact, anchored to Caesar + Africa; he defeated Scipio and Juba (Thapsus). Verifiable named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: dehinc Scipionem ac Iubam reliquias partium in Africa refouentis deuicit, Pompei liberos in Hispania.
question: Quos Caesar in Hispania, ultimo bello ciuili, deuicit?
question_en: Whom did Caesar defeat in Spain, in the last stage of the civil war?
derivation: Victory fact, anchored to Caesar + Spain; he defeated Pompey's sons (Munda). Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: ipse prosperrime semper ac ne ancipiti quidem umquam fortuna praeterquam bis dimicauit: semel ad Dyrrachium, ubi pulsus non instante Pompeio negauit eum uincere scire.
question: Quid Caesar de Pompeio dixit, cum ad Dyrrachium pulsus esset neque Pompeius instaret?
question_en: What did Caesar say about Pompey after being repulsed at Dyrrachium, when Pompey did not press on?
answer_en: That he did not know how to win.
derivation: Reported saying, anchored to Caesar + Pompey + Dyrrachium. Verbatim substance; translatable; fact-seeking. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Confectis bellis quinquiens triumphauit, post deuictum Scipionem quater eodem mense, sed interiectis diebus, et rursus semel post superatos Pompei liberos.
question: Quotiens Caesar, bellis confectis, triumphauit?
question_en: How many times did Caesar triumph after the wars were finished?
derivation: Number fact, anchored to Caesar; he celebrated five triumphs. Single number answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: primum et excellentissimum triumphum egit Gallicum, sequentem Alexandrinum, deinde Ponticum, huic proximum Africanum, nouissimum Hispaniensem.
question: Quem triumphum Caesar primum et excellentissimum egit?
question_en: Which triumph did Caesar celebrate first and as the most distinguished?
derivation: Sequence fact, anchored to Caesar; the first and finest of his five triumphs was the Gallic. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: ascenditque Capitolium ad lumina quadraginta elephantis dextra sinistraque lychnuchos gestantibus.
question: Quot elephanti lychnuchos gestantes Caesarem in triumpho Gallico Capitolium ascendentem comitati sunt?
question_en: How many lamp-bearing elephants escorted Caesar as he climbed the Capitol at his Gallic triumph?
derivation: Number fact, anchored to Caesar + the Gallic triumph; forty elephants bearing lamps escorted him up the Capitol. Single number answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: fuitque is annus, quo haec constituebantur, quindecim mensium cum intercalario, qui ex consuetudine in eum annum inciderat.
question: Quot menses habuit annus quo Caesar fastos corrigebat?
question_en: How many months did the year have in which Caesar was reforming the calendar?
derivation: The 'year of confusion' fact, anchored to Caesar's calendar reform; that year had fifteen months. Single number answer supported verbatim; distinct from the 365-day fact. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: atque ex uiginti trecentisque milibus accipientium frumentum e publico ad centum quinquaginta retraxit.
question: Ad quot milia Caesar numerum ciuium frumentum publicum accipientium redegit?
question_en: To how many thousand did Caesar reduce the number of citizens receiving the public grain dole?
derivation: Reform number, anchored to Caesar; he cut the grain-dole recipients from 320,000 to 150,000. Single number answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: omnisque medicinam Romae professos et liberalium artium doctores, quo libentius et ipsi urbem incolerent et ceteri adpeterent, ciuitate donauit.
question: Quibus Romae Caesar ciuitatem dedit, ut libentius urbem incolerent?
question_en: To whom at Rome did Caesar grant citizenship, so they would more gladly dwell in the city?
answer_en: To physicians and teachers of the liberal arts.
derivation: Policy fact, anchored to Caesar; he granted citizenship to physicians and teachers of liberal arts at Rome. Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: bibliothecas Graecas Latinasque quas maximas posset publicare data Marco Varroni cura comparandarum ac digerendarum.
question: Cui Caesar curam bibliothecas Graecas Latinasque comparandi ac digerendi mandauit?
question_en: To whom did Caesar entrust the task of acquiring and arranging Greek and Latin libraries?
derivation: Plan fact, anchored to Caesar; he gave Varro charge of the public Greek and Latin libraries. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: ualitudine prospera, nisi quod tempore extremo repente animo linqui atque etiam per somnum exterreri solebat. comitiali quoque morbo bis inter res agendas correptus est.
question: Quo morbo Caesar bis inter res agendas correptus est?
question_en: By what disease was Caesar twice seized while conducting business?
derivation: Health fact, anchored to Caesar; he was twice seized by the morbus comitialis (epilepsy). Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book, well-known.

author: Suetonius
source_text: ex omnibus decretis sibi a senatu populoque honoribus non aliud aut recepit aut usurpauit libentius quam ius laureae coronae perpetuo gestandae.
question: Quem honorem Caesar ex omnibus sibi decretis libentissime usurpauit?
question_en: Which of all the honors decreed to him did Caesar most gladly make use of?
answer_en: The right to wear the laurel crown perpetually.
derivation: Honour fact, anchored to Caesar; of all honours he most gladly used the right to wear the laurel crown always (to hide his baldness). Verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Habitauit primo in Subura modicis aedibus, post autem pontificatum maximum in Sacra uia domo publica.
question: In qua regione urbis Caesar primo modicis aedibus habitauit?
question_en: In which quarter of the city did Caesar first live, in a modest house?
derivation: Residence fact, anchored to Caesar; he first lived in the Subura, later in a state house on the Sacra Via after becoming pontifex maximus. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Britanniam petisse spe margaritarum, quarum amplitudinem conferentem interdum sua manu exegisse pondus.
question: Qua spe Caesarem Britanniam petisse Suetonius refert?
question_en: In hope of what does Suetonius report Caesar sought Britain?
derivation: Suetonian claim, anchored to Caesar + Britain; attributed frame (Suetonius refert). Single answer supported verbatim. Closed-book (a fact particular to this author).

author: Suetonius
source_text: sed ante alias dilexit Marci Bruti matrem Seruiliam, cui et proximo suo consulatu sexagiens sestertium margaritam mercatus est.
question: Quam feminam, Marci Bruti matrem, Caesar ante alias dilexit?
question_en: Which woman, the mother of Marcus Brutus, did Caesar love above all others?
derivation: Relation fact, anchored to Caesar + Servilia (mother of M. Brutus); he loved her before all others. Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: sed maxime Cleopatram ... quam denique accitam in urbem non nisi maximis honoribus praemiisque auctam remisit filiumque natum appellare nomine suo passus est.
question: Cuius reginae filium Caesar nomine suo appellari passus est?
question_en: Whose son did Caesar allow to be called by his own name?
derivation: Relation fact, anchored to Caesar + Cleopatra; he allowed her son to bear his name (Caesarion). Single named answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Vini parcissimum ne inimici quidem negauerunt. Marci Catonis est: unum ex omnibus Caesarem ad euertendam rem publicam sobrium accessisse.
question: Quid Marcus Cato de Caesare et sobrietate dixisse fertur?
answer: Vnum ex omnibus Caesarem ad euertendam rem publicam sobrium accessisse.
question_en: What did Marcus Cato say about Caesar and sobriety?
answer_en: That Caesar alone of all men came to overthrow the state sober.
derivation: Saying attributed to Cato, anchored to Caesar. Verbatim quote; translatable; fact-seeking. Closed-book, iconic.

author: Suetonius

source_text: Maiores Othonis orti sunt oppidio Ferentio, familia vetere et honorata atque ex principibus Etruriae.
question: Ex quo oppido Etruriae maiores Othonis imperatoris ortos esse Suetonius tradit?
question_en: From which town of Etruria does Suetonius say the ancestors of the emperor Otho sprang?
derivation: Origins fact. Entity-anchored to Otho + Ferentium + Etruria; place answer supported verbatim by 'Maiores Othonis orti sunt oppidio Ferentio... ex principibus Etruriae.' Indirect statement (maiores... ortos esse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: Otho's family came from Ferentium, an old and honored house among the leading families of Etruria.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Post patris deinde mortem libertinam aulicam gratiosam, quo efficacius coleret, etiam diligere simulavit quamvis anum ac paene decrepitam: per hanc insinuatus Neroni, facile summum inter amicos locum tenuit congruentia morum.
question: Cuius principis Otho, antequam ipse imperaret, summum inter amicos locum tenuisse traditur?
question_en: Of which emperor is Otho said to have held the foremost place among his friends, before he himself ruled?
derivation: Relationship fact: having insinuated himself through a court freedwoman, Otho won the foremost place among Nero's friends. Entity-anchored to Otho + Nero; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'insinuatus Neroni, facile summum inter amicos locum tenuit.' Personal passive 'tenuisse traditur.' Closed-book: Otho was a close intimate of Nero before his own accession.

author: Suetonius
source_text: item Poppaeam Sabinam tunc adhuc amicam eius, abductam marito demandatamque interim sibi, nuptiarum specie recepit, nec corrupisset contentus, adeo dilexit ut ne rivalem quidem Neronem aequo tulerit animo.
question: Quam feminam, postea Neronis uxorem, Otho marito abductam nuptiarum specie recepit, quam adeo dilexit ut ne Neronem quidem rivalem aequo animo ferret?
question_en: Which woman, later Nero's wife, did Otho receive under the guise of marriage after she had been taken from her husband, loving her so much that he could not bear even Nero as a rival?
derivation: Relationship fact: Otho received Poppaea Sabina (taken from her husband and entrusted to him) under the guise of marriage and loved her so much that he resented Nero as rival. Answer supported verbatim by 'Poppaeam Sabinam... nuptiarum specie recepit... adeo dilexit ut ne rivalem quidem Neronem aequo tulerit animo.' Entity-anchored to Otho + Poppaea + Nero. Closed-book: the famous love-triangle; Poppaea passed from Otho to Nero, whose wife she became.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Quare diducto matrimonio, sepositus est per causam legationis in Lusitaniam.
question: In quam provinciam Otho, diducto cum Poppaea matrimonio, per causam legationis sepositus est?
question_en: Into which province was Otho banished under the pretext of a legation, after his marriage with Poppaea was dissolved?
derivation: Career fact: after Nero broke up the marriage, Otho was relegated to Lusitania under cover of a governorship, which he held as ex-quaestor for ten years ('per decem annos,' same chapter). Province answer supported verbatim by 'sepositus est per causam legationis in Lusitaniam.' Entity-anchored to Otho + Lusitania. Closed-book: Otho's pre-imperial governorship of Lusitania.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ibi missis qui Galbam et Pisonem trucidarent, ad conciliandos pollicitationibus militum animos nihil magis pro contione testatus est, quam id demum se habiturum, quod sibi illi reliquissent.
question: Quos Otho, in castris imperator consalutatus, trucidandos curavit ut imperium occuparet?
question_en: Whom did Otho, after being hailed emperor in the camp, have killed in order to seize power?
derivation: Coup fact: hailed imperator in the praetorian camp, Otho dispatched men to murder Galba and his adopted heir Piso. Answer supported verbatim by 'missis qui Galbam et Pisonem trucidarent.' Entity-anchored to Otho + Galba + Piso. Closed-book: the praetorian coup of 15 January AD 69 that overthrew Galba.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ac super ceteras gratulantium adulantiumque blanditias ab infima plebe appellatus Nero nullum indicium recusantis dedit.
question: Cuius principis defuncti cognomen Otho imperator non recusavit, cum eo ab infima plebe appellaretur?
question_en: The surname of which deceased emperor did Otho not refuse, when the lowest commons hailed him by it?
derivation: Accession fact: hailed 'Nero' by the lowborn populace, Otho gave no sign of refusing, and cultivated Nero's memory (he restored his statues and recalled his freedmen). Answer supported verbatim by 'ab infima plebe appellatus Nero nullum indicium recusantis dedit.' Entity-anchored to Otho + Nero. Closed-book: Otho courted the memory and name of Nero.

author: Suetonius
