source_text: Sub idem vero tempus Germaniciani exercitus in Vitellii verba iurarat.
question: In cuius verba Germaniciani exercitus iuraverant, qui mox Othonem imperio depulit?
question_en: To whom had the armies of Germany sworn allegiance, the man who soon drove Otho from power?
derivation: Rival fact: the German legions swore allegiance to Vitellius, raising the rival who would defeat Otho. Answer supported verbatim by 'Germaniciani exercitus in Vitellii verba iurarat' (iurare in verba alicuius = to swear allegiance to). Entity-anchored to Vitellius + the German armies. Closed-book: Vitellius proclaimed emperor by the Rhine legions, AD 69.

author: Suetonius
source_text: novissimo maximoque apud Betriacum fraude superatus est, cum, spe conloquii facta, quasi ad condicionem pacis militibus eductis, ex improviso atque in ipsa consalutatione dimicandum fuisset.
question: Quo loco proelio novissimo et maximo Otho imperator superatus est, priusquam sibi mortem conscivit?
question_en: At what place was the emperor Otho defeated in the last and greatest battle, before he took his own life?
derivation: Defeat fact: Otho's decisive defeat in the last and greatest battle, at Bedriacum, by Vitellius's generals. Place answer supported verbatim by 'novissimo maximoque apud Betriacum... superatus est.' Entity-anchored to Otho + Bedriacum. Closed-book: the battle of Bedriacum decided the war against Vitellius, AD 69. (Latin Library spelling 'Betriacum' for 'Bedriacum.')

author: Suetonius
source_text: Post hoc sedata siti gelidae aquae potione, arripuit duos pugiones et explorata utriusque acie, cum alterum pulvino subdidisset, foribus adopertis artissimo somno quievit. Et circa lucem demum expergefactus, uno se traiecit ictu infra laevam papillam irrumpentibusque ad primum gemitum modo celans modo detegens plagam, exanimatus est.
question: Quomodo Otho imperator, apud Betriacum victus, vitam finivit?
question_en: How did the emperor Otho, defeated at Bedriacum, end his life?
answer_en: He stabbed himself with a dagger.
derivation: Death fact: though he could still have fought on (fresh, undefeated reserves remained, ch. 9), Otho chose to die; he stabbed himself once below the left breast with a dagger. Answer supported by 'arripuit duos pugiones... uno se traiecit ictu infra laevam papillam... exanimatus est.' Entity-anchored to Otho. Closed-book: Otho's famous dignified suicide, AD 69. (The motive of sparing further bloodshed is Suetonius's 'ut multi opinantur' gloss; the fact itself is the suicide.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: exanimatus est et celeriter (nam ita praeceperat) funeratus, tricensimo et octavo aetatis anno et nonagesimo quinto imperii die.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Otho imperator periit?
question_en: In which year of his age did the emperor Otho die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact. Ordinal answer supported verbatim by 'tricensimo et octavo aetatis anno.' Entity-anchored to Otho. Closed-book: Otho died in his thirty-eighth year (AD 69).

author: Suetonius
source_text: exanimatus est et celeriter (nam ita praeceperat) funeratus, tricensimo et octavo aetatis anno et nonagesimo quinto imperii die.
question: Quoto imperii die Otho imperator periit?
question_en: On which day of his reign did the emperor Otho die?
derivation: Reign-length fact. Number answer supported verbatim by 'nonagesimo quinto imperii die.' Entity-anchored to Otho. Closed-book: Otho's reign lasted about three months, ending on its ninety-fifth day.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Interfuit huic bello pater meus Suetonius Laetus, tertiae decimae legionis tribunus angusticlavius.
question: Quis fuit pater Suetoni, qui Othoniano bello tribunus angusticlavius legionis tertiae decimae interfuit?
question_en: Who was the father of Suetonius, who took part in the Othonian war as a narrow-stripe tribune of the thirteenth legion?
derivation: Autobiographical fact: Suetonius names his own father, Suetonius Laetus, who served in Otho's war as tribunus angusticlavius of legio XIII. Name answer supported verbatim by 'pater meus Suetonius Laetus, tertiae decimae legionis tribunus angusticlavius.' Entity-anchored to Suetonius + his father + the thirteenth legion. Closed-book: one of the few personal disclosures by Suetonius, an eyewitness source for the campaign of AD 69.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Publius Terentius Afer, Carthagine natus, serviit Romae Terentio Lucano senatori, a quo ob ingenium et formam non institutus modo liberaliter sed et mature manumissus est.
question: Ubi natus est Publius Terentius Afer?
question_en: Where was Publius Terentius Afer born?
derivation: Birthplace fact, supported verbatim ('Carthagine natus'); his cognomen 'Afer' reflects this African origin. Anchored to Terence, single place-name answer (locative-ablative 'Carthagine'), closed-book: the canonical birthplace of the comic poet.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Publius Terentius Afer, Carthagine natus, serviit Romae Terentio Lucano senatori, a quo ob ingenium et formam non institutus modo liberaliter sed et mature manumissus est.
question: A quo senatore Terentius et liberaliter institutus et manumissus est?
question_en: By which senator was Terence both liberally educated and set free?
derivation: Patron fact: the senator Terentius Lucanus owned, educated, and freed him (whence the name 'Terentius'). Supported verbatim ('serviit ... Terentio Lucano senatori, a quo ... institutus ... sed et ... manumissus est'). Entity-anchored, single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Hic cum multis nobilibus familiariter vixit, sed maxime cum Scipione Africano et C. Laelio.
question: Quibuscum duobus viris nobilibus Terentius maxime familiariter vixit?
answer: Cum Scipione Africano et C. Laelio.
question_en: With which two noblemen did Terence live on closest terms of friendship?
answer_en: With Scipio Africanus and Gaius Laelius.
derivation: His famous friendship with the young nobles Scipio Aemilianus Africanus and Gaius Laelius. Supported verbatim ('maxime cum Scipione Africano et C. Laelio'). Entity-anchored, two-name answer, closed-book staple of Terentian biography.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Scripsit comoedias sex, ex quibus primam 'Andriam' cum aedilibus daret, iussus ante Caecilio recitare.
question: Quot comoedias Terentius scripsit?
question_en: How many comedies did Terence write?
derivation: Number fact, supported verbatim ('Scripsit comoedias sex'). Anchored to Terence, single number answer; the surviving six comedies are the canonical, closed-book figure.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Scripsit comoedias sex, ex quibus primam 'Andriam' cum aedilibus daret, iussus ante Caecilio recitare.
question: Quae ex Terentii comoediis prima fuit?
question_en: Which of Terence's comedies was the first?
derivation: First-play fact, supported verbatim ('ex quibus primam Andriam'). Anchored to Terence, single-title answer, closed-book: the Andria is the well-known debut comedy.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: 'Eunuchus' quidem bis die acta est meruitque pretium quantum nulla antea cuiusquam comoedia, id est octo milia nummorum.
question: Quantum pretium comoedia 'Eunuchus' Terentii meruit?
question_en: What price did Terence's comedy Eunuchus earn?
derivation: Number fact: the Eunuchus, staged twice in one day, earned more than any earlier comedy. Supported verbatim ('meruitque pretium ... id est octo milia nummorum'). Anchored to the Eunuchus, single number answer, closed-book (the record fee for a comedy).

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Q. Cosconius redeuntem e Graecia perisse in mari dicit cum C. et VIII. fabulis conversis a Menandro.
question: Q. Cosconius unde redeuntem Terentium in mari perisse dicit?
question_en: From where, according to Q. Cosconius, was Terence returning when he perished at sea?
derivation: Death-journey fact: he died at sea returning from Greece. Supported verbatim ('redeuntem e Graecia perisse in mari'). Attributed to Cosconius ('dicit') for the closed-book 'according to this source' frame; indirect statement (redeuntem ... perisse) governed by dicit. Anchored to Terence and Greece.

author: Suetonius (Vita Terenti)
source_text: Ceteri mortuum esse in Arcadia Stymphali sive Leuccadiae tradunt Cn. Cornelio Dolabella M. Fulvio Nobiliore consulibus.
question: Quibus consulibus Terentium mortuum esse Vita tradit?
answer: Cn. Cornelio Dolabella et M. Fulvio Nobiliore.
question_en: In whose consulship does the Life record that Terence died?
answer_en: When Gnaeus Cornelius Dolabella and Marcus Fulvius Nobilior were consuls.
derivation: Death-year fact (159 BC), supported verbatim ('Cn. Cornelio Dolabella M. Fulvio Nobiliore consulibus'). Anchored to Terence, named consular pair; 'tradit' keeps the closed-book reported frame. Indirect statement (Terentium mortuum esse) under tradit.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Patricia gens Claudia--fuit enim et alia plebeia, nec potentia minor nec dignitate--orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.
question: Ex quo oppido gentem Claudiam ortam esse Suetonius tradit?
question_en: From which town does Suetonius say the Claudian gens originated?
derivation: Origin of the gens Claudia (Tiberius's family), supported verbatim by 'orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.' Indirect statement (ortam esse) under tradit; entity-anchored to the Claudii, single place answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
question: A quo patre Tiberius Caesar genus paternum traxit?
question_en: From which father did Tiberius Caesar derive his paternal line?
derivation: Names Tiberius's father, supported by 'paternum a Tiberio Nerone.' Entity-anchored to Tiberius, single named-entity answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Drusum fratrem in Germania amisit, cuius corpus pedibus toto itinere praegrediens Romam usque peruexit.
question: Ubi Drusus, Tiberii Caesaris frater, mortuus est?
question_en: Where did Drusus, the brother of Tiberius Caesar, die?
derivation: Establishes both Tiberius's brother (Drusus) and where he died, supported by 'Drusum fratrem in Germania amisit.' Entity-anchored, single place answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sed ut plures certioresque tradunt, natus est Romae in Palatio XVI. Kal. Dec. M. Aemilio Lepido iterum L. Munatio Planco conss.
question: Quibus consulibus natum esse Tiberium plures certioresque tradunt?
answer: M. Aemilio Lepido iterum et L. Munatio Planco.
question_en: In whose consulship do the more reliable sources say Tiberius was born?
answer_en: When Marcus Aemilius Lepidus (for the second time) and Lucius Munatius Plancus were consuls.
derivation: Birth-year fact (42 BC), anchored to Tiberius and the named consular pair. Indirect statement (natum esse) under tradunt; answer in the ablative matching 'M. Aemilio Lepido iterum L. Munatio Planco conss.' Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Agrippinam, Marco Agrippa genitam, neptem Caecili Attici equitis R., ad quem sunt Ciceronis epistulae, duxit uxorem.
question: Quam primam uxorem Tiberius duxit?
question_en: Whom did Tiberius take as his first wife?
derivation: Tiberius's first wife (Vipsania Agrippina), daughter of Agrippa, supported by 'Agrippinam, Marco Agrippa genitam ... duxit uxorem.' Entity-anchored, accusative answer matching the object of duxit, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: sublatoque ex ea filio Druso, quanquam bene conuenientem rursusque grauidam dimittere ac Iuliam Augusti filiam confestim coactus est ducere non sine magno angore animi.
question: Quam, Agrippina dimissa, Tiberius in matrimonium ducere coactus est?
question_en: Whom, after Agrippina was sent away, was Tiberius compelled to marry?
derivation: Tiberius was forced to divorce Agrippina and marry Augustus's daughter Iulia; supported by 'coactus est ducere ... Iuliam Augusti filiam.' Entity-anchored, accusative answer, closed-book; the compulsion is in the source (coactus est).

author: Suetonius
source_text: dein ducto ad Orientem exercitu regnum Armeniae Tigrani restituit ac pro tribunali diadema imposuit.
question: Cui regi Tiberius regnum Armeniae restituit?
question_en: To which king did Tiberius restore the kingdom of Armenia?
derivation: Supported by 'regnum Armeniae Tigrani restituit.' Entity-anchored to Tiberius + Armenia, single dative-named answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: recepit et signa, quae M. Crasso ademerant Parthi.
question: A quo populo Tiberius signa recepit, quae M. Crasso erepta erant?
question_en: From which people did Tiberius recover the standards that had been taken from Marcus Crassus?
derivation: Recovery of the standards lost by Crassus (at Carrhae), supported by 'signa, quae M. Crasso ademerant Parthi.' Entity-anchored (Crassus, Parthians, standards), single answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sed increbrescente rumore quasi ad occasionem maioris spei commoraretur, tantum non aduersis tempestatibus Rhodum enauigauit, amoenitate et salubritate insulae iam inde captus cum ad eam ab Armenia rediens appulisset.
question: Quo Tiberius integra aetate sponte secessit, insulae amoenitate captus?
question_en: Where did Tiberius voluntarily withdraw to in the prime of life, captivated by the island's charm?
derivation: Tiberius's famous self-imposed retirement (ch. 10: 'statuit repente secedere'); the destination Rhodes is supported by 'Rhodum enauigauit, amoenitate et salubritate insulae ... captus.' Entity-anchored, single place answer, closed-book and iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Gaio et Lucio intra triennium defunctis adoptatur ab Augusto simul cum fratre eorum M. Agrippa, coactus prius ipse Germanicum fratris sui filium adoptare.
question: A quo Tiberius, Gaio et Lucio Caesaribus mortuis, in adoptionem ascitus est?
question_en: By whom was Tiberius adopted after the deaths of Gaius and Lucius Caesar?
derivation: Tiberius (Augustus's stepson) was adopted by Augustus after Gaius and Lucius died; supported by 'adoptatur ab Augusto.' Entity-anchored, single answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Gaio et Lucio intra triennium defunctis adoptatur ab Augusto simul cum fratre eorum M. Agrippa, coactus prius ipse Germanicum fratris sui filium adoptare.
question: Cuius filium Tiberius, antequam ipse ab Augusto adoptaretur, adoptare coactus est?
question_en: Whose son was Tiberius compelled to adopt before he himself was adopted by Augustus?
answer_en: Germanicus, the son of his brother.
derivation: As a condition of his own adoption, Tiberius first adopted Germanicus, son of his brother Drusus; supported by 'coactus prius ipse Germanicum fratris sui filium adoptare.' Entity-anchored, accusative answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: praesidibus onerandas tributo prouincias suadentibus rescripsit boni pastoris esse tondere pecus, non deglubere.
question: Quid Tiberius praesidibus rescripsit, qui prouincias tributo onerandas esse suadebant?
answer: Boni pastoris esse tondere pecus, non deglubere.
question_en: What did Tiberius write back to the governors who urged that the provinces be burdened with tribute?
answer_en: That it is a good shepherd's part to shear his flock, not to flay it.
derivation: Tiberius's famous saying on taxation, supported verbatim. Fact-seeking (which reply, to which petition) and entity-anchored; the maxim has a short, translatable, verifiable point. Answer mirrors the source's acc.+inf.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Capreas se contulit, praecipue delectatus insula, quod uno paruoque litore adiretur, saepta undique praeruptis immensae altitudinis rupibus et profundo mari.
question: In quam insulam Tiberius se contulit, ubi reliquam uitam in secessu egit?
question_en: To which island did Tiberius betake himself, where he spent the rest of his life in seclusion?
derivation: Tiberius's later withdrawal to Capri, supported by 'Capreas se contulit, praecipue delectatus insula.' Entity-anchored, single place answer, closed-book and iconic.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Statimque reuocante assidua obtestatione populo propter cladem, qua apud Fidenas supra uiginti hominum milia gladiatorio munere amphitheatri ruina perierant, transiit in continentem.
question: Quot fere hominum milia apud Fidenas ruina amphitheatri perierunt?
question_en: About how many thousand people perished at Fidenae in the collapse of the amphitheatre?
derivation: The Fidenae amphitheatre collapse (AD 27), supported by 'apud Fidenas supra uiginti hominum milia ... amphitheatri ruina perierant.' Number + place fact, entity-anchored, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sed tempestatibus et ingrauescente ui morbi retentus paulo post obiit in uilla Lucullana octauo et septuagesimo aetatis anno, tertio et uicesimo imperii, XVII. Kal. Ap. Cn. Acerronio Proculo C. Pontio Nigrino conss.
question: Quoto aetatis anno Tiberius mortuus est?
question_en: In which year of his age did Tiberius die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact (AD 37), supported by 'octauo et septuagesimo aetatis anno.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored, closed-book. (source_text normalizes the edition's 'Nigr[in]o' to 'Nigrino'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Sed tempestatibus et ingrauescente ui morbi retentus paulo post obiit in uilla Lucullana octauo et septuagesimo aetatis anno, tertio et uicesimo imperii, XVII. Kal. Ap. Cn. Acerronio Proculo C. Pontio Nigrino conss.
question: Quoto imperii anno Tiberius decessit?
question_en: In which year of his reign did Tiberius die?
derivation: Length-of-reign fact, supported by 'tertio et uicesimo imperii.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Tiberius, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Corpus ut moueri a Miseno coepit, conclamantibus plerisque Atellam potius deferendum et in amphitheatro semiustilandum, Romam per milites deportatum est crematumque publico funere.
question: In quo loco Tiberius decessit, unde corpus eius Romam deportatum est?
question_en: In what place did Tiberius die, from which his body was carried to Rome?
derivation: Place of death: his body was carried from Misenum ('Corpus ut moueri a Miseno coepit ... Romam ... deportatum est'), establishing he died there (the Lucullan villa of ch. 73). Entity-anchored, single place answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Eo testamento heredes aequis partibus reliquit Gaium ex Germanico et Tiberium ex Druso nepotes substituitque in uicem.
question: Quos nepotes Tiberius testamento heredes aequis partibus reliquit?
answer: Gaium, ex Germanico, et Tiberium, ex Druso.
question_en: Which grandsons did Tiberius leave as equal heirs in his will?
answer_en: Gaius, son of Germanicus, and Tiberius, son of Drusus.
derivation: Tiberius's will named two grandsons as equal heirs; supported verbatim. Gaius (Caligula) became his successor, Tiberius being Gemellus. Entity-anchored, accusative answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Titus cognomine paterno, amor ac deliciae generis humani, (tantum illi ad promerendam omnium voluntatem vel ingenii vel artis vel fortunae superfuit, et, quod difficillimum est, in imperio: quando privatus atque etiam sub patre principe ne odio quidem, nedum vituperatione publica caruit), natus est III. Kal. Ian.
question: Quo praeconio Suetonius Titum imperatorem in vitae principio appellat?
question_en: By what acclamation does Suetonius hail the emperor Titus at the start of his life?
answer_en: The love and darling of the human race.
derivation: The famous Suetonian judgment on Titus. Supported verbatim by the appositive 'amor ac deliciae generis humani.' Entity-anchored to Titus; closed-book, as this is among the most quoted epithets of any emperor. Answer cast in accusative as the predicate of appellat.

author: Suetonius
source_text: educatus in aula cum Britannico simul, ac paribus disciplinis et apud eosdem magistros institutus.
question: Cum quo Titus in aula educatus est, paribus disciplinis et apud eosdem magistros institutus?
question_en: With whom was Titus brought up in the palace, schooled in the same studies under the same teachers?
answer_en: With Britannicus (son of the emperor Claudius).
derivation: Biographical fact: Titus was reared alongside Britannicus, Claudius's son. Supported verbatim by 'educatus in aula cum Britannico simul.' Entity-anchored to Titus + Britannicus; single-name answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: eodemque tempore Arrecinam Tertullam, patre eq. R. sed praefecto quodam praetorianarum cohortium, duxit uxorem et in defunctae locum Marciam Furnillam splendidi generis; cum qua, sublata filia, divortium fecit.
question: Quas uxores Titus duxit, primum unam, deinde in defunctae locum alteram?
question_en: Which wives did Titus marry, one first and then a second in place of the deceased?
derivation: Family fact: the two wives of Titus. Supported verbatim by 'Arrecinam Tertullam ... duxit uxorem et in defunctae locum Marciam Furnillam.' Entity-anchored to Titus; bounded two-name answer (cf. the multi-name set answers in the Vespasian file).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ex questurae deinde honore legioni praepositus, Taricheas et Gamalam urbes Iudaeae validissimas in potestate redegit.
question: Quas urbes Iudaeae validissimas Titus, legioni praepositus, in potestatem redegit?
question_en: Which very strong cities of Judaea did Titus, put in command of a legion, bring under his power?
derivation: Career fact from the Jewish war. Supported verbatim by 'Taricheas et Gamalam urbes Iudaeae validissimas in potestate redegit.' Entity-anchored to Titus + Judaea; two named-place answer. (source_text keeps the Latin Library reading 'in potestate redegit' for 'in potestatem redegit.')

author: Suetonius
source_text: Cuius brevi compos, et ad perdomandam Iudaeam relictus, novissima Hierosolymorum oppugnatione duodecim propugnatores totidem sagittarum confecit ictibus, cepitque ea natali filiae suae tanto militum gaudio ac favore, ut in gratulatione imperatorem eum consalutaverint.
question: Quam urbem Titus, ad perdomandam Iudaeam relictus, novissima oppugnatione cepit?
question_en: Which city did Titus, left to subdue Judaea, capture in the final assault?
derivation: The famous conquest: Titus took Jerusalem in the final assault of the Jewish war (AD 70). Supported by 'novissima Hierosolymorum oppugnatione ... cepitque ea.' Entity-anchored to Titus + Jerusalem; single-place answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Triumphavit cum patre censuramque gessit una, eidem collega et in tribunicia potestate et in septem consulatibus fuit.
question: In quot consulatibus Titus patri Vespasiano collega fuit?
question_en: In how many consulships was Titus a colleague to his father Vespasian?
derivation: Number/office fact: Titus shared seven consulships with his father. Supported verbatim by 'in septem consulatibus fuit.' Entity-anchored to Titus + Vespasian; single-number answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Berenicen statim ab urbe dimisit, invitus, invitam.
question: Quam reginam Titus, princeps factus, statim ab urbe dimisit, invitus invitam?
question_en: Which queen did Titus, on becoming emperor, immediately send away from Rome, unwilling though she too was unwilling?
derivation: Famous episode: Titus dismissed Queen Berenice from Rome on his accession. Supported verbatim by 'Berenicen statim ab urbe dimisit, invitus, invitam.' Entity-anchored to Titus + Berenice; single-name answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Et tamen nemine ante se munificentia minor, amphitheatro dedicato thermisque iuxta celeriter exstructis, munus edidit apparatissimum largissimusque; dedit et navale proelium in veteri naumachia, ibidem et gladiatores atque uno die quinque milia omne genus ferarum.
question: Quod opus Titus dedicavit, thermis iuxta celeriter exstructis, cum munus apparatissimum ederet?
question_en: What structure did Titus dedicate, with baths quickly built nearby, when he gave a most lavish show?
answer_en: The amphitheatre (the Flavian Amphitheatre, the Colosseum).
derivation: Building fact: Titus dedicated the amphitheatre (the Colosseum) and built adjacent baths. Supported verbatim by 'amphitheatro dedicato thermisque iuxta celeriter exstructis.' Entity-anchored to Titus; single-answer; the most famous act of his reign.

author: Suetonius
source_text: atque etiam recordatus quondam super cenam, quod nihil cuiquam toto die praestitisset, memorabilem illam meritoque laudatam vocem edidit: "Amici, diem perdidi."
question: Quam memorabilem vocem Titus edidit, cum recordatus esset se nihil cuiquam toto die praestitisse?
question_en: What memorable saying did Titus utter when he recalled that he had done no one a kindness the whole day?
answer_en: Friends, I have lost a day.
derivation: The most famous saying of Titus. Supported verbatim by the quoted 'Amici, diem perdidi.' Entity-anchored to Titus; survives translation; closed-book. Indirect statement (se ... praestitisse) under recordatus esset.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Quaedam sub eo fortuita ac tristia acciderunt, ut conflagratio Vesevi montis in Campania, et incendium Romae per triduum totidemque noctes, item pestilentia quanta non temere alias.
question: Cuius montis conflagratio in Campania sub Tito principe accidit?
question_en: The eruption of which mountain occurred in Campania during the reign of Titus?
derivation: The eruption of Vesuvius (AD 79), the great disaster of Titus's reign. Supported verbatim by 'conflagratio Vesevi montis in Campania.' Entity-anchored to Titus's reign + Campania; single-place answer; closed-book. (source_text keeps the Latin Library spelling 'Vesevi' for 'Vesuvii'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Pontificatum maximum ideo se professus accipere ut puras servaret manus, fidem praestitit.
question: Quod sacerdotium Titus se accipere professus est, ut puras servaret manus?
question_en: Which priesthood did Titus profess to take up in order to keep his hands clean?
answer_en: The office of pontifex maximus (chief priesthood).
derivation: Office fact: Titus said he accepted the pontificate maximus to keep his hands pure. Supported verbatim by 'Pontificatum maximum ideo se professus accipere ut puras servaret manus.' Entity-anchored to Titus; single-office answer; indirect statement (se accipere) under professus.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Fratrem insidiari sibi non desinentem, sed paene ex professo sollicitantem exercitus, meditantem fugam, neque occidere neque seponere ac ne in minore quidem honore habere sustinuit, sed, ut a primo imperii die, consorte successoremque testari perseveravit.
question: Quem Titus, quamvis sibi insidiantem, a primo imperii die consortem ac successorem imperii testari perseveravit?
question_en: Whom did Titus, although he kept plotting against him, persist in declaring his partner and successor in the empire from the first day of his reign?
derivation: Succession fact: Titus persisted in naming his brother (Domitian, who did succeed him) as partner and heir despite his plotting. Supported by 'Fratrem ... consorte successoremque testari perseveravit'; the brother of Titus is Domitian. Entity-anchored to Titus + Domitian; closed-book. (source_text keeps the Latin Library reading 'consorte' for 'consortem'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit in eadem qua pater villa Id. Septb. post biennium ac menses duos diesque XX. quam successerat patri, altero et quadragesimo aetatis anno.
question: Cui Titus in principatu successit?
question_en: Whom did Titus succeed as emperor?
derivation: Succession fact: Titus succeeded his father. Supported verbatim by 'quam successerat patri'; the father of Titus is Vespasian. Entity-anchored to Titus; single-name answer; closed-book (the Flavian succession).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit in eadem qua pater villa Id. Septb. post biennium ac menses duos diesque XX. quam successerat patri, altero et quadragesimo aetatis anno.
question: In qua villa Titus mortuus est?
question_en: In what villa did Titus die?
answer_en: In the same villa as his father (the Sabine villa at Aquae Cutiliae).
derivation: Death-place fact: Titus died in the same villa as his father Vespasian (Aquae Cutiliae in the Sabine country; cf. 'Sabinos petiit' in ch. 10). Supported verbatim by 'Excessit in eadem qua pater villa.' Entity-anchored to Titus; place answer; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit in eadem qua pater villa Id. Septb. post biennium ac menses duos diesque XX. quam successerat patri, altero et quadragesimo aetatis anno.
question: Quamdiu Titus, postquam patri successit, imperium tenuit?
answer: Biennium ac menses duos diesque viginti.
question_en: How long did Titus hold power after he had succeeded his father?
answer_en: Two years, two months, and twenty days.
derivation: Reign-length fact. Supported verbatim by 'post biennium ac menses duos diesque XX. quam successerat patri.' Entity-anchored to Titus; precise duration answer (accusative of extent); closed-book (his famously short reign).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Excessit in eadem qua pater villa Id. Septb. post biennium ac menses duos diesque XX. quam successerat patri, altero et quadragesimo aetatis anno.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Titus decessit?
question_en: In which year of his age did Titus die?
derivation: Age-at-death fact. Supported verbatim by 'altero et quadragesimo aetatis anno.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Titus; closed-book (he died in AD 81, in his early forties).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Rebellione trium principum et caede incertum diu et quasi vagum imperium suscepit firmavitque tandem gens Flavia, obscura illa quidem ac sine ullis maiorum imaginibus, sed tamen rei p. nequaquam paenitenda.
question: Quae gens, ut Suetonius scribit, imperium diu incertum ac vagum tandem suscepit firmavitque?
question_en: Which family, as Suetonius writes, finally took up and made firm the empire that had long been uncertain and adrift?
derivation: The founding of the Flavian dynasty (Vespasian, then his sons Titus and Domitian). Anchored to the gens Flavia; single-entity answer supported verbatim by 'suscepit firmavitque tandem gens Flavia.' Closed-book: the rise of the Flavians after the year of the four emperors.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Vespasianus natus est in Sabinis ultra Reate vico modico, cui nomen est Phalacrinae, XV. kal. Dec. vesperi, Q. Sulpicio Camerino C. Poppaeo Sabino cons., quinquennio ante quam Augustus excederet.
question: Quo in loco, in Sabinis ultra Reate, Vespasianum natum esse Suetonius tradit?
answer: In vico cui nomen Phalacrinae, ultra Reate.
question_en: In what place, in the Sabine country beyond Reate, does Suetonius say Vespasian was born?
answer_en: In the village called Phalacrinae, beyond Reate.
derivation: Birthplace fact, anchored to Vespasian. Supported verbatim by 'in Sabinis ultra Reate vico modico, cui nomen est Phalacrinae.' Indirect statement (natum esse) under tradit. Closed-book: Vespasian's Sabine birthplace near Reate is a standard biographical fact.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Postea faenus apud Helvetios exercuit ibique diem obiit superstitibus uxore Vespasia Polla et duobus ex ea liberis, quorum maior Sabinus ad praefecturam urbis, minor Vespasianus ad principatum usque processit.
question: Quo nomine appellata est mater Vespasiani imperatoris?
question_en: By what name was the mother of the emperor Vespasian called?
derivation: Family fact. The source names Vespasia Polla as the wife (of Vespasian's father) and mother of the two sons, of whom the younger, Vespasian, reached the principate. Entity-anchored to Vespasian; single-name answer supported verbatim.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Inter haec Flaviam Domitillam duxit uxorem, Statilii Capellae equitis R. Sabratensis ex Africa delicatam olim Latinaeque condicionis, sed mox ingenuam et civem Rom. reciperatorio iudicio pronuntiatam.
question: Quam Vespasianus uxorem duxit, ex qua liberos suscepit?
question_en: Whom did Vespasian take as his wife, from whom he had his children?
derivation: Family fact. Supported verbatim by 'Flaviam Domitillam duxit uxorem.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian; single-name answer. Closed-book: his wife, mother of Titus and Domitian.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ex hac liberos tulit Titum et Domitianum et Domitillam.
question: Quos liberos Vespasianus ex Flavia Domitilla tulit?
question_en: What children did Vespasian have by Flavia Domitilla?
derivation: Family fact. Supported verbatim by 'Ex hac liberos tulit Titum et Domitianum et Domitillam.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian and Flavia Domitilla; the two sons, Titus and Domitian, each later became emperor. Short list answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: inde in Britanniam translatus tricies cum hoste conflixit. Duas validissimas gentes superque viginti oppida et insulam Vectem Britanniae proximan in dicionem redegit, partim Auli Plautii legati consularis, partim Claudi ipsius ductu.
question: Quam insulam Britanniae proximam Vespasianus, in Britannia rem gerens, in dicionem redegit?
question_en: Which island next to Britain did Vespasian, while campaigning in Britain, bring under his control?
answer_en: The island of Vectis (the Isle of Wight).
derivation: Career fact: under Claudius, Vespasian campaigned in Britain and subdued the island of Vectis (Isle of Wight). Supported verbatim by 'insulam Vectem Britanniae proximan in dicionem redegit.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian + Britain + the named island; single place answer. (source_text retains the Latin Library OCR slip 'proximan' for 'proximam'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Additis igitur ad copias duabus legionibus, octo alis, cohortibus decem, atque inter legatos maiore filio assumpto, ut primum provinciam attigit, proximas quoque convertit in se.
question: Quem filium suum Vespasianus, dux in bello Iudaico, inter legatos sibi assumpsit?
question_en: Which of his sons did Vespasian, as commander in the Jewish war, take to himself among his legates?
derivation: Career fact: in the Jewish war (under Nero) Vespasian took his elder son Titus among his legates. Supported by 'inter legatos maiore filio assumpto'; the elder son is Titus (named ch. 3). Entity-anchored to Vespasian + Titus + the Jewish war; short answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: et unus ex nobilibus captivis Iosephus, cum coiceretur in vincula, constantissime asseveravit fore ut ab eodem brevi solveretur, verum iam imperatore.
question: Quis ex nobilibus captivis, in vincula coniectus, Vespasianum brevi imperatorem fore praedixit?
question_en: Which of the noble captives, when thrown into chains, predicted that Vespasian would soon be emperor?
derivation: Famous anecdote: the captured Jewish leader Josephus declared that Vespasian would soon free him, but as emperor. Supported by 'unus ex nobilibus captivis Iosephus ... asseveravit fore ut ab eodem brevi solveretur, verum iam imperatore.' Entity-anchored to Josephus + Vespasian; single-name answer; closed-book (a well-known episode of Josephus's life).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Ceterum divulgato facto, Tiberius Alexander praefectus Aegypti primus in verba Vespasiani legiones adegit Kal. Iul., qui principatus dies in posterum observatus est.
question: Quis praefectus Aegypti primus legiones in verba Vespasiani adegit?
question_en: Which prefect of Egypt was the first to swear his legions into allegiance to Vespasian?
derivation: Accession fact (AD 69). Supported verbatim by 'Tiberius Alexander praefectus Aegypti primus in verba Vespasiani legiones adegit Kal. Iul.'; that day (1 July) was thereafter kept as Vespasian's dies imperii. Entity-anchored, single-name answer; the proclamation of Vespasian while in the East.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Talis tantaque cum fama in urbem reversus, acto de Iudaeis triumpho, consulatus octo veteri addidit; suscepit et censuram.
question: De qua gente Vespasianus, in urbem reversus, triumphum egit?
question_en: Over what people did Vespasian, on returning to the city, celebrate a triumph?
derivation: Career fact: the Jewish triumph (AD 71). Supported verbatim by 'acto de Iudaeis triumpho.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian + the Jews; short answer. Closed-book: the famous triumph over Judaea, commemorated on the Arch of Titus.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Fecit et nova opera templum Pacis foro proximum, Divique Claudii in Caelio monte coeptum quidem ab Agrippina, sed a Nerone prope funditus destructum; item amphitheatrum urbe media, ut destinasse compererat Augustum.
question: Quod novum opus Vespasianus urbe media exstruere coepit, quod Augustum destinasse compererat?
question_en: What new structure did Vespasian begin to build in the middle of the city, which he had learned Augustus had planned?
answer_en: An amphitheatre (the Flavian Amphitheatre, the Colosseum).
derivation: Building fact: the Flavian Amphitheatre (Colosseum), begun by Vespasian in the city center. Supported verbatim by 'item amphitheatrum urbe media.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian; single answer; the most famous Flavian monument.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Reprehendenti filio Tito, quod etiam urinae vectigal commentus esset, pecuniam ex prima pensione admovit ad nares, sciscitans num odore offenderetur; et illo negante: Atqui, inquit, e lotio est.
question: Quid Vespasianus filio Tito respondit, cum is urinae vectigal a patre excogitatum reprehenderet?
question_en: What did Vespasian reply to his son Titus, when Titus criticized the tax on urine devised by his father?
answer_en: And yet it comes from urine.
derivation: The iconic 'pecunia non olet' episode: Titus objected to the urine tax, and Vespasian held a coin to his nose, saying 'Atqui, e lotio est' ('And yet it's from urine'). Supported verbatim. Entity-anchored to Vespasian + Titus + the urine tax; the saying survives translation and is among the most famous in Suetonius.

author: Suetonius
source_text: prima quoque morbi accessione: Vae, inquit, puto, deus fio.
question: Quid Vespasianus per iocum dixit, cum primum morbo, quo postea periit, corriperetur?
question_en: What did Vespasian jokingly say when he was first seized by the illness of which he later died?
answer_en: Woe, I think I am becoming a god.
derivation: Vespasian's dying jest at the onset of his final illness, mocking the deification of emperors. Supported verbatim by 'prima quoque morbi accessione: Vae, inquit, puto, deus fio.' Entity-anchored to Vespasian; the famous saying survives translation; closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: alvo repente usque ad defectionem soluta, imperatorem, ait statem mori oportere; dumque consurgit ac mititur, inter manus sublevantium extinctus est VIIII. Kal. Iul.
question: Quid Vespasianus moriens dixit imperatorem facere oportere?
question_en: What did the dying Vespasian say an emperor ought to do?
answer_en: Die standing (an emperor ought to die on his feet).
derivation: Vespasian's last famous saying, that an emperor ought to die standing; he died in the act of rising, held up by his attendants. Entity-anchored to Vespasian; translatable; closed-book. (source_text retains the Latin Library OCR slips 'statem' for 'stantem' and 'mititur' for 'nititur'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Consulatu suo nono temptatus in Campania motiunculis levibus protinusque urbe repetita, Cutilias ac Reatina rura, ubi aestivare quotannis solebat, petit.
question: Quo Vespasianus, valetudine temptatus, ex urbe se contulit, ubi mox decessit?
question_en: To what place did Vespasian, when his health failed, withdraw from the city, where he soon died?
answer_en: To Cutiliae and the Reatine country (near Reate).
derivation: Death-place fact: Vespasian fell ill and died at Cutiliae (Aquae Cutiliae) in the Reatine country near Reate, his usual summer retreat. Supported verbatim by 'Cutilias ac Reatina rura ... petit'; he died there (ch. 24, 'inter manus sublevantium extinctus est'). Entity-anchored; place answer.

author: Suetonius
source_text: inter manus sublevantium extinctus est VIIII. Kal. Iul. annum agens aetatis sexagensimum ac nonum, superque mensem ac diem septimum.
question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Vespasianus decessit, ut Suetonius tradit?
question_en: In which year of his age did Vespasian die, according to Suetonius?
derivation: Age-at-death fact. Supported verbatim by 'annum agens aetatis sexagensimum ac nonum.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Vespasian; closed-book (he died in AD 79, aged 69). (source_text retains the Latin Library spelling 'sexagensimum' for 'sexagesimum'.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Convenit inter omnis, tam certum eum de sua suorumque genitura semper fuisse, ut post assiduas in se coniurationes ausus sit adfirmare senatui, ut filios sibi successuros aut neminem.
question: Quos Vespasianus senatui adfirmavit sibi successuros esse aut neminem?
question_en: Whom did Vespasian declare to the senate would succeed him, or else no one would?
derivation: Succession fact: Vespasian assured the senate that his sons would succeed him or no one. Supported verbatim by 'filios sibi successuros aut neminem'; his sons Titus, then Domitian, did in fact succeed him. Entity-anchored to Vespasian; short answer.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Natus est Gn. Pompeio Magno M. Licinio Crasso primum conss. Iduum Octobrium die in pago qui Andes dicitur et abest a Mantua non procul.
question: Quibus consulibus Vergilius natus est?
answer: Gn. Pompeio Magno et M. Licinio Crasso.
question_en: In whose consulship was Vergil born?
answer_en: When Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus and Marcus Licinius Crassus were consuls.
derivation: Birth-year fact (70 BC), anchored to Vergil and the named consular pair, supported verbatim by 'Gn. Pompeio Magno M. Licinio Crasso primum conss.' Closed-book: one of the canonical dates of Latin literary biography.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Natus est Gn. Pompeio Magno M. Licinio Crasso primum conss. Iduum Octobrium die in pago qui Andes dicitur et abest a Mantua non procul.
question: In quo pago prope Mantuam Vergilius natus esse traditur?
question_en: In what village near Mantua is Vergil said to have been born?
derivation: Birthplace fact, anchored to Vergil and Mantua, supported verbatim ('in pago qui Andes dicitur et abest a Mantua non procul'). Indirect statement (natus esse) under traditur. Andes near Mantua is the iconic, closed-book birthplace.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Initia aetatis Cremonae egit usque ad virilem togam, quam XV anno natali suo accepit iisdem illis consulibus iterum duobus, quibus erat natus, evenitque ut eo ipso die Lucretius poeta decederet.
question: Quis poeta eo ipso die decessit quo Vergilius togam virilem accepit?
question_en: Which poet died on the very day that Vergil assumed the toga of manhood?
derivation: The famous coincidence: Lucretius died the day Vergil took the toga virilis. Supported verbatim ('eo ipso die Lucretius poeta decederet'). Entity-anchored (Vergil, Lucretius), single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Cetera sane vitae et ore et animo tam probum constat, ut Neapoli Parthenias vulgo appellatus sit.
question: Quo cognomine Vergilius Neapoli vulgo appellatus est?
question_en: By what nickname was Vergil commonly called at Naples?
derivation: His nickname for his pure life, supported verbatim ('Neapoli Parthenias vulgo appellatus sit'). Anchored to Vergil and Naples, single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: quorum maxime dilexit Cebetem et Alexandrum, quem secunda 'Bucolicorum' egloga Alexim appellat, donatum sibi ab Asinio Pollione.
question: Quod erat verum nomen pueri quem Vergilius in secunda Bucolicorum egloga Alexim appellat?
question_en: What was the real name of the boy whom Vergil calls Alexis in the second Eclogue?
derivation: Standard Vergilian-biography fact: the Alexis of Eclogue 2 is Alexander. Supported verbatim ('Alexandrum, quem secunda Bucolicorum egloga Alexim appellat'). Anchored to Vergil and the Eclogue, single-name answer, closed-book literary detail.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: 'Bucolica' triennio, 'Georgica' VII, 'Aeneida' XI perfecit annis.
question: Quot annis Vergilius Bucolica perfecit, ut Vita tradit?
question_en: In how many years did Vergil complete the Eclogues, according to the Life?
derivation: Number fact, supported verbatim ('Bucolica triennio'). Anchored to Vergil and the Bucolica; one of the textbook figures (3/7/11 years) for his three works. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: 'Bucolica' triennio, 'Georgica' VII, 'Aeneida' XI perfecit annis.
question: Quot annis Vergilius Georgica perfecit, ut Vita tradit?
question_en: In how many years did Vergil complete the Georgics, according to the Life?
derivation: Number fact, supported verbatim ('Georgica VII ... perfecit annis'). Anchored to Vergil and the Georgica, single number answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: 'Bucolica' triennio, 'Georgica' VII, 'Aeneida' XI perfecit annis.
question: Quot annis Vergilius Aeneida perfecit, ut Vita tradit?
question_en: In how many years did Vergil complete the Aeneid, according to the Life?
derivation: Number fact, supported verbatim ('Aeneida XI perfecit annis'). Anchored to Vergil and the Aeneid, single number answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Deinde scripsit 'Georgica' in honorem Maecenatis, qui sibi mediocriter adhuc noto opem tulisset adversus veterani cuiusdam violentiam.
question: In cuius honorem Vergilius Georgica scripsit?
question_en: In whose honor did Vergil write the Georgics?
derivation: Dedicatee fact, supported verbatim ('Georgica in honorem Maecenatis'). Anchored to Vergil and the Georgica, single-name answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: 'Aeneida' prosa prius oratione formatam digestamque in XII libros particulatim componere instituit.
question: In quot libros Vergilius Aeneida digessit?
question_en: Into how many books did Vergil arrange the Aeneid?
derivation: Number fact, supported verbatim ('digestam ... in XII libros'). Anchored to Vergil and the Aeneid, single number answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Cui tamen multo post perfectaque demum materia tres omnino libros recitavit, secundum, quartum et sextum.
question: Quos tres Aeneidos libros Vergilius Augusto recitavit?
question_en: Which three books of the Aeneid did Vergil recite to Augustus?
answer_en: The second, the fourth, and the sixth.
derivation: Vergil recited three books to Augustus (the 'Cui' = Augustus, requesting the poem in the previous sentence). Supported verbatim ('tres omnino libros recitavit, secundum, quartum et sextum'). Entity-anchored, short list answer, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: tres omnino libros recitavit, secundum, quartum et sextum, sed hunc notabili Octaviae adfectione, quae cum recitationi interesset, ad illos de filio suo versus, 'tu Marcellus eris,' defecisse fertur atque aegre focilata est.
question: Quibus versibus de Marcello auditis Octavia, Vergilio recitante, defecisse fertur?
question_en: On hearing which verse about Marcellus is Octavia said to have fainted while Vergil was reciting?
derivation: The famous scene: Octavia faints at the Marcellus lines in Aeneid 6. Supported verbatim ('ad illos de filio suo versus, tu Marcellus eris, defecisse fertur'). Anchored to Octavia, Marcellus and Vergil; 'defecisse fertur' mirrors the source's reported frame.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: 'Aeneidos' vixdum coeptae tanta exstitit fama, ut Sextus Propertius non dubitaverit sic praedicare: 'Cedite, Romani scriptores, cedite Grai: Nescio quid maius nascitur Iliade.'
question: Quis poeta de nascente Aeneide praedicavit 'nescio quid maius nascitur Iliade'?
question_en: Which poet declared of the nascent Aeneid, 'something greater than the Iliad is being born'?
derivation: Famous reception line, supported verbatim and attributed to 'Sextus Propertius.' Entity-anchored (Propertius, the Aeneid/Iliad), single-name answer; the quotation 'maius ... Iliade' is iconic and closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: languorem nactus est eumque non intermissa navigatione auxit ita ut gravior aliquanto Brundisium appelleret, ubi diebus paucis obiit XI Kal. Octobr. Cn. Sentio Q. Lucretio conss.
question: In quo oppido Vergilius mortuus est?
question_en: In what town did Vergil die?
derivation: Place-of-death fact, supported verbatim ('Brundisium appelleret, ubi ... obiit'). Anchored to Vergil, single place answer, closed-book famous.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: languorem nactus est eumque non intermissa navigatione auxit ita ut gravior aliquanto Brundisium appelleret, ubi diebus paucis obiit XI Kal. Octobr. Cn. Sentio Q. Lucretio conss.
question: Quibus consulibus Vergilius Brundisii decessit?
question_en: In whose consulship did Vergil die at Brundisium?
answer_en: When Gnaeus Sentius and Quintus Lucretius were consuls.
derivation: Death-date fact (19 BC), supported verbatim ('Cn. Sentio Q. Lucretio conss.'). Anchored to Vergil and Brundisium, named consular pair, closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Ossa eius Neapolim translata sunt tumuloque condita qui est via Puteolana intra lapidem secundum.
question: Quo Vergilii ossa post mortem translata sunt?
question_en: Where were Vergil's bones taken after his death?
derivation: Burial-place fact, supported verbatim ('Ossa eius Neapolim translata sunt'); the tomb stood on the via Puteolana within the second milestone. Anchored to Vergil, single place answer, closed-book famous.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Mantua me genuit, Calabri rapuere, tenet nunc Parthenope; cecini pascua rura duces.
question: Quae tria se cecinisse Vergilius in epitaphio suo dicit?
question_en: What three things does Vergil say in his epitaph that he sang?
answer_en: Pastures, fields, and leaders (the Eclogues, Georgics, and Aeneid).
derivation: The famous epitaph ('Mantua me genuit ...') names his three works as 'pascua rura duces.' Supported verbatim, short list answer; the line is iconic and closed-book, the answer translatable (the three subjects = his three poems).

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Heredes fecit ex dimidia parte Valerium Proculum fratrem alio patre, ex quarta Augustum, ex duodecima Maecenatem, ex reliqua L. Varium et Plotium Tuccam, qui eius 'Aeneida' post obitum iussu Caesaris emendaverunt.
question: Qui Vergilii Aeneida post eius obitum iussu Augusti emendaverunt?
question_en: Who edited Vergil's Aeneid after his death by order of Augustus?
derivation: Literary-executor fact, supported verbatim ('L. Varium et Plotium Tuccam, qui eius Aeneida post obitum iussu Caesaris emendaverunt'); Caesar here = Augustus. Entity-anchored, two-name answer, iconic and closed-book.

author: Suetonius (Vita Vergilii)
source_text: Egerat cum Vario, priusquam Italia decederet, ut siquid sibi accidisset, 'Aeneida' combureret; at is ita facturum se pernegarat.
question: Quem Vergilius rogaverat ut, si quid sibi accidisset, Aeneida combureret?
question_en: Whom had Vergil asked to burn the Aeneid if anything should happen to him?
derivation: The famous wish to have the Aeneid burned, supported verbatim ('Egerat cum Vario ... ut ... Aeneida combureret'). Anchored to Vergil and Varius, single-name answer; Varius refused. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Advenientem male animatus erga principem exercitus pronusque ad res novas libens ac supinis manibus excepit, velut dono deum oblatum, ter consulis filium, aetate integra, facili ac prodigo animo.
question: Quotiens consul fuit pater A. Vitellii imperatoris?
question_en: How many times was the father of the emperor Aulus Vitellius consul?
derivation: Family fact: the emperor's father, Lucius Vitellius, was consul three times (AD 34, 43, 47). The army welcomed Vitellius as 'ter consulis filium' (son of a man thrice consul). Number answer supported verbatim by 'ter consulis filium.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius's father; closed-book: Lucius Vitellius's three consulships are the standard mark of his eminence under Claudius.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Lucius ex consulatu Syriae praepositus, Artabanum Parthorum regem summis artibus non modo ad conloquium suum, sed etiam ad veneranda legionum signa pellexit. Mox cum Claudio principe duos insuper ordinarios consulatus censuramque gessit.
question: Quod munus Lucius Vitellius, A. Vitellii imperatoris pater, cum Claudio principe praeter consulatus gessit?
question_en: What office, besides consulships, did Lucius Vitellius, the father of the emperor Aulus Vitellius, hold together with the emperor Claudius?
derivation: Family/career fact: Lucius Vitellius held the censorship (AD 47-48) jointly with Claudius, along with two further ordinary consulships. Answer supported verbatim by 'duos insuper ordinarios consulatus censuramque gessit.' Entity-anchored to Lucius Vitellius + Claudius; single-office answer. Closed-book: Lucius Vitellius was Claudius's colleague in the censorship.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Decessit paralysi altero die quam correptus est, duobus filiis superstitibus, quos ex Sextilia probatissima nec ignobili femina editos consules vidit, et quidem eodem ambos totoque anno, cum maiori minor in sex menses successisset.
question: Quae fuit mater A. Vitellii imperatoris?
question_en: Who was the mother of the emperor Aulus Vitellius?
derivation: Family fact: Sextilia, wife of Lucius Vitellius, was the mother of the emperor. The source records that Lucius's two surviving sons were born 'ex Sextilia' and both reached the consulship in one year (the younger succeeding the elder within six months) - the elder being the future emperor Aulus Vitellius. Single-name answer supported verbatim by 'ex Sextilia ... editos.' Entity-anchored to the emperor; closed-book: Sextilia is the known mother of Vitellius (cf. ch. 14, his suspected role in her death).

author: Suetonius
source_text: Trium itaque principium indulgentia non solum honoribus verum et sacerdotiis amplissimis auctus, proconsulatum Africae post haec curamque operum publicorum administravit et voluntate dispari et existimatione.
question: Cuius provinciae proconsulatum A. Vitellius ante principatum administravit?
question_en: Of which province did Aulus Vitellius hold the proconsulship before his reign?
derivation: Career fact: before becoming emperor Vitellius governed Africa as proconsul. Province answer supported verbatim by 'proconsulatum Africae ... administravit.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius + Africa; verifiable, translatable, fact-seeking. Closed-book: a fixed point of his pre-imperial cursus.

author: Suetonius
source_text: A Galba in inferiorem Germaniam contra opinionem missus est.
question: In quam provinciam A. Vitellius a Galba missus est?
question_en: To which province was Aulus Vitellius sent by Galba?
derivation: Pivotal fact: Galba sent Vitellius, against expectation, to govern Lower Germany (Germania Inferior), where the legions soon proclaimed him emperor. Place answer supported verbatim by 'A Galba in inferiorem Germaniam ... missus est.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius + Galba + Lower Germany. Closed-book: the command from which Vitellius launched his bid for the throne in AD 69.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Consentiente deinde etiam superioris provinciae exercitu, qui prius a Galba ad senatum defecerat, cognomen Germanici delatum ab universis cupide recepit, Augusti distulit, Caesaris in perpetuum recusavit.
question: Quod cognomen A. Vitellius ab exercitu oblatum cupide recepit?
question_en: Which cognomen, offered by the army, did Aulus Vitellius eagerly accept?
derivation: Accession fact: on his proclamation Vitellius eagerly took the cognomen 'Germanicus' (from his German legions), deferred 'Augustus,' and refused 'Caesar.' Answer supported verbatim by 'cognomen Germanici ... cupide recepit.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius; single-name answer. Closed-book: 'Germanicus' is the title by which Vitellius styled himself.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Consentiente deinde etiam superioris provinciae exercitu, qui prius a Galba ad senatum defecerat, cognomen Germanici delatum ab universis cupide recepit, Augusti distulit, Caesaris in perpetuum recusavit.
question: Quod nomen A. Vitellius, imperator a militibus consalutatus, in perpetuum recusavit?
question_en: Which name did Aulus Vitellius, hailed emperor by the soldiers, refuse forever?
derivation: Accession fact: while accepting 'Germanicus,' Vitellius refused the name 'Caesar' outright and for good - an unusual gesture among the emperors. Answer supported verbatim by 'Caesaris in perpetuum recusavit.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius; translatable, fact-seeking. Closed-book: a noted detail of his accession.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Hanc quoque exsuperavit ipse dedicatione patinae, quam ob immensam magnitudinem clipeum Minervae polioychoy dictitabat.
question: Quo nomine A. Vitellius patinam illam immensae magnitudinis appellabat?
question_en: By what name did Aulus Vitellius call that platter of enormous size?
answer_en: The shield of Minerva the city-protectress (Poliouchos).
derivation: Gluttony fact (single clean datum): a colossal dish Vitellius nicknamed 'the shield of Minerva Poliouchos' (city-guardian). Answer supported verbatim by 'clipeum Minervae ... dictitabat.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius; translatable as a nickname. Closed-book: the 'Shield of Minerva' is the most famous emblem of his legendary gluttony. (source_text keeps the Latin Library transliteration 'polioychoy' for Greek poliouchou.)

author: Suetonius
source_text: Octavo imperii mense desciverunt ab eo exercitus Moesiarum atque Pannoniae, item ex transmarinis Iudaicus et Syriaticus, ac pars in absentis, pars in praesentis Vespasiani verba iurarunt.
question: Quoto imperii mense exercitus Moesiarum et Pannoniae ab A. Vitellio desciverunt?
question_en: In which month of his reign did the armies of the Moesias and of Pannonia revolt from Aulus Vitellius?
derivation: Reign-length anchor: in the eighth month of his reign the Danubian and eastern armies revolted; Vitellius held power only about eight months (proclaimed Jan., dead Dec. AD 69). Ordinal answer supported verbatim by 'Octavo imperii mense desciverunt.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Octavo imperii mense desciverunt ab eo exercitus Moesiarum atque Pannoniae, item ex transmarinis Iudaicus et Syriaticus, ac pars in absentis, pars in praesentis Vespasiani verba iurarunt.
question: In cuius verba exercitus, ab A. Vitellio deficientes, iurarunt?
question_en: To whom did the armies that revolted from Aulus Vitellius swear allegiance?
derivation: Succession fact: the revolting armies (Moesia, Pannonia, Judaea, Syria) swore allegiance to Vespasian. Answer supported verbatim by '... in ... Vespasiani verba iurarunt' (idiom iurare in verba alicuius). Entity-anchored to Vitellius + Vespasian. Closed-book: Vespasian's bid that overthrew Vitellius and ended the year of the four emperors.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Tandem apud Gemonias minutissimis ictibus excarnificatus atque confectus et inde unco tractus in Tiberim.
question: In quod flumen cadaver A. Vitellii unco tractum est?
question_en: Into which river was the body of Aulus Vitellius dragged with a hook?
derivation: Death fact: tortured to death with tiny cuts at the Gemonian steps, Vitellius's body was then dragged with a hook into the Tiber. Place answer supported verbatim by 'unco tractus in Tiberim.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius. Closed-book: the infamous end of Vitellius.

author: Suetonius
source_text: Periit cum fratre et filio anno vitae septimo quinquagesimo.
question: Quotum vitae annum agens A. Vitellius, ut Suetonius tradit, periit?
question_en: In which year of his life did Aulus Vitellius die, as Suetonius reports?
derivation: Age-at-death fact: he died in his fifty-seventh year. Ordinal answer supported verbatim by 'anno vitae septimo quinquagesimo.' Attributed to Suetonius ('ut Suetonius tradit') because this figure is the author's (the age is debated). Entity-anchored to Vitellius. Closed-book.

author: Suetonius
source_text: siquidem ab Antonio Primo adversarum partium duce oppressus est, cum Tolosae nato cognomen in pueritia Becco fuerat; id valet gallinacei rostrum.
question: A quo adversarum partium duce A. Vitellius oppressus est?
question_en: By which leader of the opposing (Flavian) party was Aulus Vitellius overthrown?
derivation: Fall fact: the Flavian general Antonius Primus crushed Vitellius. Name answer supported verbatim by 'ab Antonio Primo adversarum partium duce oppressus est.' Entity-anchored to Vitellius + Antonius Primus. Closed-book: Antonius Primus led Vespasian's forces to the decisive victory (second battle of Bedriacum/Cremona, Oct. AD 69).

author: Tacitus
source_text: Hic interim liber honori Agricolae soceri mei destinatus, professione pietatis aut laudatus erit aut excusatus.
question: Qua necessitudine Gnaeus Iulius Agricola cum Tacito coniunctus fuit?
question_en: By what family relationship was Gnaeus Julius Agricola connected to Tacitus?
derivation: Tacitus calls Agricola 'soceri mei' (my father-in-law), the work being dedicated to his honor. Anchored to two named persons; single verifiable relation; the famous frame of the whole biography. Tacitus married Agricola's daughter, so Agricola is his socer.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Gnaeus Iulius Agricola, vetere et inlustri Foroiuliensium colonia ortus, utrumque avum procuratorem Caesarum habuit, quae equestris nobilitas est.
question: In qua colonia Gnaeus Iulius Agricola ortus est?
question_en: In which colony was Gnaeus Julius Agricola born?
answer_en: In the colony of Forum Iulii.
derivation: Agricola's birthplace, stated verbatim as 'Foroiuliensium colonia ortus'. Anchored to the named person; single place answer; the canonical opening fact of the biography.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Pater illi Iulius Graecinus senatorii ordinis, studio eloquentiae sapientiaeque notus, iisque ipsis virtutibus iram Gai Caesaris meritus: namque Marcum Silanum accusare iussus et, quia abnuerat, interfectus est.
question: Quis fuit pater Agricolae?
question_en: Who was Agricola's father?
derivation: Names Agricola's father ('Pater illi Iulius Graecinus'). Anchored to Agricola; single named answer supported verbatim; closed-book biographical fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Mater Iulia Procilla fuit, rarae castitatis.
question: Quae fuit mater Agricolae?
question_en: Who was Agricola's mother?
derivation: Names Agricola's mother ('Mater Iulia Procilla fuit'). Anchored to Agricola; single named answer verbatim in source.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Hinc ad capessendos magistratus in urbem degressus Domitiam Decidianam, splendidis natalibus ortam, sibi iunxit; idque matrimonium ad maiora nitenti decus ac robur fuit.
question: Quam feminam Agricola in matrimonium duxit?
question_en: Which woman did Agricola marry?
derivation: Agricola's wife, named in 'Domitiam Decidianam... sibi iunxit'. Anchored to Agricola; single named answer; closed-book relation fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Revertentem ab legatione legionis divus Vespasianus inter patricios adscivit; ac deinde provinciae Aquitaniae praeposuit, splendidae inprimis dignitatis administratione ac spe consulatus, cui destinarat.
question: Cui provinciae divus Vespasianus Agricolam praeposuit?
question_en: Over which province did the deified Vespasian place Agricola?
derivation: Named office/province: Vespasian set Agricola over Aquitania ('provinciae Aquitaniae praeposuit'). Anchored to Vespasian + Agricola; single province answer verbatim.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Hanc oram novissimi maris tunc primum Romana classis circumvecta insulam esse Britanniam adfirmavit, ac simul incognitas ad id tempus insulas, quas Orcadas vocant, invenit domuitque.
question: Quid Romana classis, oram novissimi maris circumvecta, tum primum adfirmavit?
question_en: What did the Roman fleet, having sailed around the coast of the farthest sea, then for the first time affirm?
derivation: The classic discovery under Agricola's governorship: the circumnavigating fleet confirmed Britain is an island ('insulam esse Britanniam adfirmavit'). Indirect statement (acc.+inf.) answer supported verbatim; entity-anchored to Britannia + the Roman fleet; one of the most-cited facts of the Agricola.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Hanc oram novissimi maris tunc primum Romana classis circumvecta insulam esse Britanniam adfirmavit, ac simul incognitas ad id tempus insulas, quas Orcadas vocant, invenit domuitque.
question: Quas insulas, antea incognitas, Romana classis Britanniam circumvecta invenit domuitque?
question_en: Which previously unknown islands did the Roman fleet discover and subdue while sailing around Britain?
derivation: Distinct fact from the same sentence: the fleet discovered and subdued the Orcades ('insulas, quas Orcadas vocant, invenit domuitque'). Anchored to the Roman fleet's circumnavigation; single named-islands answer verbatim.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Igitur primus omnium Romanorum divus Iulius cum exercitu Britanniam ingressus, quamquam prospera pugna terruerit incolas ac litore potitus sit, potest videri ostendisse posteris, non tradidisse.
question: Quis primus omnium Romanorum cum exercitu Britanniam ingressus est?
question_en: Who was the first of all Romans to enter Britain with an army?
derivation: States verbatim that Julius Caesar was 'primus omnium Romanorum' to enter Britain with an army. Single named answer; closed-book, much-cited historical fact; anchored to Britannia + the Romans.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Consularium primus Aulus Plautius praepositus ac subinde Ostorius Scapula, uterque bello egregius: redactaque paulatim in formam provinciae proxima pars Britanniae, addita insuper veteranorum colonia.
question: Quis primus ex consularibus Britanniae praepositus est?
question_en: Who was the first of the consulars placed in charge of Britain?
derivation: Named office/relation: 'Consularium primus Aulus Plautius praepositus'. Anchored to Britannia; single named answer verbatim; closed-book.

author: Tacitus
source_text: His atque talibus in vicem instincti, Boudicca generis regii femina duce (neque enim sexum in imperiis discernunt) sumpsere universi bellum.
question: Qua femina duce Britanni adversus Romanos universi bellum sumpserunt?
question_en: Under which woman as leader did the Britons all together take up war against the Romans?
derivation: Names the leader of the British revolt, 'Boudicca generis regii femina duce'. Anchored to the Britons + Romans; single named answer verbatim (spelled 'Boudicca' in the text); famous, closed-book.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Igitur praemissa classe, quae pluribus locis praedata magnum et incertum terrorem faceret, expedito exercitu, cui ex Britannis fortissimos et longa pace exploratos addiderat, ad montem Graupium pervenit, quem iam hostis insederat.
question: Ad quem montem Agricola pervenit, ubi postremum cum Britannis proelium commisit?
question_en: To what mountain did Agricola come, where he fought his final battle with the Britons?
derivation: The climactic battle's site, 'ad montem Graupium pervenit'. Anchored to Agricola + the Britons; single named-place answer verbatim; the canonical battle of the Agricola.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Iamque super triginta milia armatorum aspiciebantur, et adhuc adfluebat omnis iuventus et quibus cruda ac viridis senectus, clari bello et sua quisque decora gestantes, cum inter pluris duces virtute et genere praestans nomine Calgacus apud contractam multitudinem proelium poscentem in hunc modum locutus fertur.
question: Quis dux Britannorum, virtute et genere praestans, ante proelium ad montem Graupium orationem habuisse fertur?
question_en: Which leader of the Britons, outstanding in valor and birth, is said to have delivered a speech before the battle at Mons Graupius?
derivation: Names the Caledonian leader, 'nomine Calgacus'. Anchored to the Britons + Mons Graupius; single named answer verbatim. The question concerns only the speaker's identity (a fact), not the rhetorical content of the speech. 'fertur... locutus' mirrors the source's report-frame; closed-book and famous.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Caesa hostium ad decem milia: nostrorum trecenti sexaginta cecidere, in quis Aulus Atticus praefectus cohortis, iuvenili ardore et ferocia equi hostibus inlatus.
question: Quot Romani in proelio ad montem Graupium ceciderunt, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: How many Romans fell in the battle at Mons Graupius, as Tacitus records?
derivation: Number fact: Roman dead at Mons Graupius, 'nostrorum trecenti sexaginta cecidere' (against about 10,000 of the enemy). Anchored to the named battle; single number answer verbatim; 'ut Tacitus tradit' marks the closed-book authorial frame.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Urbem Romam a principio reges habuere; libertatem et consulatum L. Brutus instituit.
question: Qui Urbem Romam a principio habuerunt, ut initio Annalium Tacitus scribit?
question_en: Who held the city of Rome at the beginning, as Tacitus writes at the opening of the Annals?
derivation: The famous opening sentence of the Annals. Anchored to the city of Rome + Tacitus's opening; single verifiable answer 'reges', supported verbatim by 'Urbem Romam a principio reges habuere'. Direct question, indicative habuerunt (= habuere); closed-book because it is among the most-quoted openings in Latin literature.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Urbem Romam a principio reges habuere; libertatem et consulatum L. Brutus instituit.
question: Quis Romae libertatem et consulatum instituisse a Tacito traditur?
question_en: Who, according to Tacitus, is said to have established liberty and the consulship at Rome?
derivation: From the same opening sentence. Anchored to Rome + the founding of the Republic; single named person, supported verbatim by 'libertatem et consulatum L. Brutus instituit'. Nominative-and-infinitive (instituisse ... traditur). Closed-book: L. Brutus as founder of liberty and the consulship is a stock fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: at hercule Germanicum Druso ortum octo apud Rhenum legionibus inposuit adscirique per adoptionem a Tiberio iussit
question: Quot legionibus apud Rhenum Germanicum Augustus imposuisse traditur?
question_en: Over how many legions at the Rhine is Augustus reported to have placed Germanicus?
derivation: Anchored to Augustus + Germanicus + the Rhine; single number, supported verbatim by 'octo apud Rhenum legionibus inposuit'. Nominative-and-infinitive (Augustus ... imposuisse traditur). Closed-book number fact about the German command Augustus gave Germanicus.

author: Tacitus
source_text: at hercule Germanicum Druso ortum octo apud Rhenum legionibus inposuit adscirique per adoptionem a Tiberio iussit
question: A quo per adoptionem Germanicum, Augusti iussu, adscitum esse Tacitus tradit?
question_en: By whom, at Augustus's command, does Tacitus report that Germanicus was adopted?
derivation: Anchored to Germanicus + Augustus; single named person, supported verbatim by 'adscirique per adoptionem a Tiberio iussit'. Indirect statement (Germanicum adscitum esse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: Germanicus's adoption by Tiberius is a stock fact of Julio-Claudian succession.

author: Tacitus
source_text: vixdum ingressus Illyricum Tiberius properis matris litteris accitur; neque satis conpertum est, spirantem adhuc Augustum apud urbem Nolam an exanimem reppererit.
question: In qua urbe Augustum mortuum esse Tacitus tradit?
question_en: In what city does Tacitus report that Augustus died?
derivation: Anchored to Augustus; single place, supported by 'Augustum apud urbem Nolam' (where Tiberius found him dying or dead); corroborated in 1.9 ('Nolae in domo et cubiculo in quo pater eius Octavius vitam finivisset'). Indirect statement (Augustum mortuum esse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: Augustus's death at Nola is a stock fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Primum facinus novi principatus fuit Postumi Agrippae caedes
question: Quod fuit primum facinus novi principatus Tiberii, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: What was the first crime of the new principate of Tiberius, as Tacitus reports?
derivation: Anchored to the new principate of Tiberius; single named event/person, supported verbatim by 'Primum facinus novi principatus fuit Postumi Agrippae caedes'. Direct question, indicative fuit. Closed-book: the killing of Agrippa Postumus as Tiberius's first act is a well-known fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Hic rerum urbanarum status erat, cum Pannonicas legiones seditio incessit, nullis novis causis nisi quod mutatus princeps licentiam turbarum et ex civili bello spem praemiorum ostendebat. castris aestivis tres simul legiones habebantur, praesidente Iunio Blaeso.
question: Quis tribus Pannonicis legionibus, cum seditionem fecerunt, praeerat, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: Who was in command of the three Pannonian legions when they mutinied, per Tacitus?
derivation: Anchored to the Pannonian legions + their mutiny (AD 14); single named legate, supported verbatim by 'tres simul legiones habebantur, praesidente Iunio Blaeso'. praeerat takes dative (legionibus). Closed-book: Blaesus is the named commander of the Pannonian mutiny.

author: Tacitus
source_text: duo apud ripam Rheni exercitus erant: cui nomen superiori sub C. Silio legato, inferiorem A. Caecina curabat.
question: Quis inferiorem apud ripam Rheni exercitum curabat, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: Who commanded the lower army on the bank of the Rhine, per Tacitus?
derivation: Anchored to the lower Rhine army (vs. the upper army under C. Silius); single named person, supported verbatim by 'inferiorem A. Caecina curabat'. Direct question, indicative curabat. Closed-book among readers of the Germanicus campaigns.

author: Tacitus
source_text: sed Varus fato et vi Armini cecidit
question: Cuius vi Varum cecidisse Tacitus tradit?
question_en: By whose force does Tacitus say Varus fell?
derivation: Anchored to Varus + Arminius; single named person, supported verbatim by 'Varus fato et vi Armini cecidit' (genitive 'Armini' as in the text). Indirect statement (Varum cecidisse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: Arminius as the destroyer of Varus is among the best-known facts of Roman history.

author: Tacitus
source_text: inerant feminae nobiles, inter quas uxor Arminii eademque filia Segestis
question: Cuius filia erat uxor Arminii, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: Whose daughter was the wife of Arminius, per Tacitus?
derivation: Anchored to Arminius + Segestes; single named relation, supported verbatim by 'uxor Arminii eademque filia Segestis'. Corroborated in 1.55 (Arminius had carried off Segestes's daughter, betrothed to another). Closed-book: that Arminius's wife was Segestes's daughter is a recurring fact in the Germanicus narrative.

author: Tacitus
source_text: iam infans in castris genitus, in contubernio legionum eductus, quem militari vocabulo Caligulam appellabant, quia plerumque ad concilianda vulgi studia eo tegmine pedum induebatur.
question: Quo militari vocabulo Germanici filium, in castris genitum, milites appellabant, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: By what military nickname did the soldiers call Germanicus's son, born in the camp, per Tacitus?
derivation: Anchored to Germanicus's son + the soldiers; single name, supported verbatim by 'quem militari vocabulo Caligulam appellabant'. Caligulam accusative as object of appellabant. Closed-book: Gaius's army-nickname 'Caligula' (from the caliga) is among the most famous facts of the period.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Bructeros sua urentis expedita cum manu L Stertinius missu Germanici fudit; interque caedem et praedam repperit undevicesimae legionis aquilam cum Varo amissam.
question: Cuius legionis aquilam, cum Varo amissam, L. Stertinius apud Bructeros repperit, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: The eagle of which legion, lost with Varus, did Stertinius recover among the Bructeri, per Tacitus?
derivation: Anchored to Stertinius + the Varus disaster + the Bructeri; single numbered legion, supported verbatim by 'repperit undevicesimae legionis aquilam cum Varo amissam'. Direct question, indicative repperit. Closed-book: the recovery of the lost eagle of the 19th legion is a notable, specific fact.

author: Tacitus
source_text: ductum inde agmen ad ultimos Bructerorum, quantumque Amisiam et Lupiam amnis inter vastatum, haud procul Teutoburgiensi saltu in quo reliquiae Vari legionumque insepultae dicebantur.
question: In quo saltu reliquias Vari legionumque insepultas iacuisse Tacitus tradit?
question_en: In what forest does Tacitus report that the unburied remains of Varus and his legions lay?
derivation: Anchored to Varus + his legions; single named place, supported verbatim by 'haud procul Teutoburgiensi saltu in quo reliquiae Vari legionumque insepultae dicebantur'. Indirect statement (reliquias ... iacuisse) governed by tradit. Closed-book: the Teutoburg Forest is the famous site of the Varian disaster.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Igitur Romanus qui aderat exercitus sextum post cladis annum trium legionum ossa, nullo noscente alienas reliquias an suorum humo tegeret, omnis ut coniunctos, ut consanguineos, aucta in hostem ira, maesti simul et infensi condebant.
question: Quot legionum ossa exercitus Germanici, sexto post Varianam cladem anno, in saltu Teutoburgiensi humo texit, ut Tacitus tradit?
question_en: The bones of how many legions did Germanicus's army bury in the Teutoburg forest, in the sixth year after the Varian disaster, per Tacitus?
derivation: The famous toll of the Varian disaster. Anchored to Germanicus's army + the Teutoburg battlefield; single number, supported verbatim by 'sextum post cladis annum trium legionum ossa ... condebant'. The clades is the defeat of Varus (cf. 1.60 'aquilam cum Varo amissam', 1.61 'Vari castra ... trium legionum manus'). Closed-book: the loss of three legions under Varus is among the best-known facts of Roman history.

author: Tacitus
source_text: Isdem consulibus ludi saeculares octingentesimo post Romam conditam, quarto et sexagesimo quam Augustus ediderat, spectati sunt.
question: Quoto anno post Romam conditam ludi saeculares, Claudio principe, spectati sunt?
question_en: In which year after the founding of Rome were the Secular Games held, in the reign of Claudius?
derivation: Anchored to the ludi saeculares + Claudius; single number answer, supported verbatim by 'ludi saeculares octingentesimo post Romam conditam ... spectati sunt'. Closed-book: Claudius's celebration of the Secular Games in the 800th year of Rome (AD 47) is a well-known event of his reign. 'Quoto anno' takes the ablative of time.

author: Tacitus
source_text: At Claudius matrimonii sui ignarus et munia censoria usurpans, theatralem populi lasciviam severis edictis increpuit.
question: Quod munus Claudius gerebat, cum theatralem populi lasciviam severis edictis increparet?
question_en: What office was Claudius holding when he rebuked the theatrical license of the people with stern edicts?
derivation: Anchored to Claudius; single office answer, supported verbatim by 'munia censoria usurpans'. Closed-book: that Claudius held the censorship (AD 47-48, with L. Vitellius) is a stock fact of his reign. 'cum ... increparet' is cum-circumstantial with the subjunctive.

author: Tacitus
